title.zh: 卷一百三十三 列傳第七十一: 叛臣 張覺子:僅言 耶律餘睹 窩斡
title.en: Volume 133 Biographies 71: Pan Chen, Zhang Jue son: Jinyan, Ye Luyudu, Wo Wo
title.raw: 卷一百三十三 列傳第七十一: 叛臣 張覺子:僅言 耶律餘睹 窩斡 Volume 133 Biographies 71: Pan Chen, Zhang Jue son: Jinyan, Ye Luyudu, Wo Wo

sentences.zh: 古書「畔」與「叛」通，畔之為言界也。

translations.literal: In ancient texts the character pan (畔) and pan (叛, 'rebel') are interchangeable; pan in this sense means 'boundary.'
translations.idiomatic: In older writings, pan (畔) and pan (叛, 'rebel') are used interchangeably; the word pan here means 'boundary.'

sentences.zh: 《左氏》曰，政猶「農之有畔」，是也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says, 'Government is like the farmer having his field boundaries'—that is the point.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary puts it this way: government is like a farmer keeping to his field boundaries—and that is the sense intended here.

sentences.zh: 君臣上下之定分，猶此疆彼界之截然，違此向彼，即為叛矣。

translations.literal: The fixed roles of ruler and subject, superior and inferior, are like this field and that boundary sharply divided; to cross from this side to that is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The settled order between ruler and subject, superior and inferior, is like a hard line between one field and the next; to step across from one side to the other is to rebel.

sentences.zh: 善惡判于跬步，禍患極於懷襄，吁，可畏哉！

translations.literal: Good and evil are decided in a single step; calamity reaches the extreme of the Huai and Xiang floods—ah, how dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil turn on a single step, and disaster can swell to the scale of the Huai and Xiang deluge—how terrifying!

sentences.zh: 作《叛臣傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore these 'Biographies of Rebel Officials' were composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence these biographies of rebel officials.

sentences.zh: 張覺，亦書作鐧，平州義豐人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue—also written with the character for 'iron mace'—was a native of Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue, whose name is also written with the character for 'iron mace,' came from Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在遼第進士，仕至遼興軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He placed as jinshi in the Liao examinations and rose to deputy military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree under the Liao and eventually served as deputy military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕京，時立愛以平州降，當時宋人以海上之盟求燕京及西京地，太祖以燕京、涿、易、檀、順、景、薊與之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor secured Yanjing, Shili Ai surrendered Ping Prefecture. At that time the Song, invoking the maritime alliance, sought Yanjing and the Western Capital territories; the Taizu Emperor gave them Yanjing together with Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu Emperor took Yanjing, Shili Ai surrendered Ping Prefecture. The Song, citing the maritime alliance, pressed for Yanjing and the Western Capital lands; the Taizu Emperor ceded Yanjing along with Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 平州自入契丹別為一軍，故弗與，而以平州為南京，覺為留守。

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture, since entering Khitan control, had been a separate army district, so it was not given over; instead Ping was made the Southern Capital and Jue was appointed resident commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Prefecture had formed its own army district under Khitan rule, so it was not handed to the Song; the Jin made it the Southern Capital instead and appointed Jue resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既而聞覺有異志，上遣使劉彥宗及斜缽諭之，詔曰：「平山一郡今為南京，節度使今為留守。

translations.literal: Before long it was heard that Jue harbored disloyal intentions. The emperor sent envoys Liu Yanzong and Xiebo to instruct him, with an edict saying: 'The single commandery of Pingshan is now the Southern Capital; the military commissioner is now the resident commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Jue was nursing disloyal designs. The emperor sent Liu Yanzong and Xiebo to admonish him with an edict: 'The Pingshan commandery is now the Southern Capital, and the post of military commissioner is now resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 恩亦厚矣。

translations.literal: Our favor has already been generous.
translations.idiomatic: Our favor toward you has already been ample.

sentences.zh: 或言汝等陰有異圖，何為當此農時輒相扇動，非去危就安之計也。

translations.literal: Some say you secretly harbor other designs—why, at this season of farming, do you stir people up? That is not a plan to leave danger and seek safety.
translations.idiomatic: Some report that you are plotting in secret—why stir unrest in the middle of the planting season? That is hardly a course that leads from danger to safety.

sentences.zh: 其諭朕意。」

translations.literal: Convey my meaning to them.'
translations.idiomatic: Make my intentions clear to them.'

sentences.zh: 太祖每收城邑，往往徙其民以實京師，民心多不安，故時立愛因降表曾言及之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Taizu Emperor took a city or town he often moved its people to fill the capital, and popular hearts were largely unsettled; therefore Shili Ai had mentioned this in his surrender memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Taizu Emperor captured a city he would often relocate its people to swell the capital, leaving the populace deeply uneasy—something Shili Ai had already raised in his surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 及以燕京與宋而遷其人，獨以空城與之，遷者道出平州，故覺因之以作亂。

translations.literal: When Yanjing was given to the Song its population was relocated, and only an empty city was handed over; those being moved passed through Ping Prefecture on the road, so Jue took advantage of this to raise a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanjing was ceded to the Song its inhabitants were relocated, leaving only an empty city behind; the evacuees had to pass through Ping Prefecture, and Jue seized on their grievances to launch a revolt.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年五月，左企弓、虞仲文、曹勇義、康公弼赴廣甯，過平州，覺使人殺之于栗林下，遂據南京叛入于宋，宋人納之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Tianfu, Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were traveling to Guangning and passed through Ping Prefecture; Jue had men kill them beneath the chestnut grove, then seized the Southern Capital, rebelled, and went over to the Song, and the Song received him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu year seven, Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were bound for Guangning and passed through Ping Prefecture. Jue had them killed under the chestnut grove, seized the Southern Capital, defected to the Song, and was welcomed by the Song court.

sentences.zh: 太祖下詔諭南京官吏，詔曰：「朕初駐蹕燕京，嘉爾吏民率先降附，故升府治以為南京，減徭役，薄賦稅，恩亦至矣，何苦輒為叛逆？

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor issued an edict instructing the officials of the Southern Capital, saying: 'When I first halted my carriage at Yanjing, I praised your officials and people for being the first to submit; therefore I raised this prefectural seat to be the Southern Capital, reduced corvée labor, and lightened taxes—our favor has already reached its utmost. Why must you suffer rebellion for no reason?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor addressed the Southern Capital officials with an edict: 'When I first made Yanjing my base, I honored your officials and people for leading the way in submission. I elevated this seat to the Southern Capital, eased corvée burdens, and cut taxes—our grace could hardly go further. Why court rebellion at such cost?

sentences.zh: 今欲進兵攻取，時方農月，不忍以一惡人而害及眾庶。

translations.literal: Now I wish to advance troops to take the city, but it is the farming season and I cannot bear to let one wicked man bring harm upon the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I am ready to march and take the city, yet the planting season is upon us, and I will not let one villain's crime visit suffering on the common people.

sentences.zh: 且遼國舉為我有，孤城自守，終欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover the entire Liao state has become mine—what can you hope to achieve by holding a lone city?
translations.idiomatic: The whole Liao realm is already mine; what end do you imagine by clinging to a single walled town?

sentences.zh: 今止坐首惡，餘並釋之。」

translations.literal: Now only the chief culprit will be punished; all the rest will be released.'
translations.idiomatic: Only the ringleader will be held to account; everyone else will go free.'

sentences.zh: 覺兵五萬屯潤州近郊，欲脅遷、來、潤、隰四州。

translations.literal: Jue had fifty thousand troops camped in the suburbs near Run Prefecture, intending to coerce the four prefectures of Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jue stationed fifty thousand troops in the outskirts near Run Prefecture, hoping to intimidate Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi into submission.

sentences.zh: 闍母自錦州往討之，已敗覺兵，欲乘勝攻南京，時暑雨不可進，退屯於海堧。

translations.literal: Chanmu marched from Jin Prefecture to attack him, already having defeated Jue's army and wishing to press the victory against the Southern Capital; at the time summer rains made advance impossible, so he withdrew and encamped at Haichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chanmu marched from Jin Prefecture to suppress him. He had already routed Jue's forces and meant to press on to the Southern Capital, but summer rains blocked the advance, so he fell back and encamped at Haichuan.

sentences.zh: 無何，闍母再敗覺兵，復與戰於兔耳山，闍母大敗，覺報捷于宋。

translations.literal: Before long Chanmu again defeated Jue's army, but when they fought once more at Rabbit-Ear Mountain Chanmu suffered a great defeat; Jue reported victory to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chanmu routed Jue's troops again, yet at Rabbit-Ear Mountain he met a crushing defeat. Jue sent word of victory to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 宋建平州為泰寧軍，以覺為節度使，張敦固等皆加徽猶閣待制，以銀絹數萬犒軍。

translations.literal: The Song established Ping Prefecture as the Taiping Army command, appointed Jue military commissioner, promoted Zhang Dungu and others to Huayou Pavilion academicians, and rewarded the army with tens of thousands in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Song reorganized Ping Prefecture as the Taiping Army district, made Jue its military commissioner, promoted Zhang Dungu and others to Huayou Pavilion academicians, and sent tens of thousands in silver and silk to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 宗望軍至南京城東，覺兵大敗宵遁，遂奔宋，入於燕京。

translations.literal: Zongwang's army reached the east of the Southern Capital city; Jue's troops were utterly defeated and fled by night, then he fled to the Song and entered Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang's army reached the eastern side of the Southern Capital, Jue's forces were shattered and fled under cover of night. He defected to the Song and took refuge in Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 宗望以納叛責宋宣撫司，索張覺。

translations.literal: Zongwang charged the Song Pacification Commission with harboring a rebel and demanded Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang accused the Song Pacification Commission of sheltering a rebel and demanded that Zhang Jue be handed over.

sentences.zh: 宣撫王安中匿之於甲仗庫，紿曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong hid him in the armory and deceived them, saying, 'He is not here.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong hid him in the armory and lied: 'We do not have him.

sentences.zh: 宗望索愈急，安中乃斬貌類覺者一人當之，金人識之曰：「非覺也。」

translations.literal: Zongwang pressed his demand ever more urgently; Anzhong then beheaded a man who resembled Jue and offered him in his place. The Jurchens recognized the deception and said, 'This is not Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang's demands grew fiercer, so Anzhong beheaded a look-alike and tried to pass him off as Jue. The Jurchens saw through it at once: 'That is not Jue.

sentences.zh: 安中不得已，引覺出。

translations.literal: With no alternative, Anzhong brought Jue out.
translations.idiomatic: Left with no choice, Anzhong produced Jue.

sentences.zh: 數以罪，覺罵宋人不容口，遂殺覺函其首以與金人。

translations.literal: His crimes were enumerated; Jue cursed the Song without pause, so they killed him, boxed his head, and gave it to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: When his crimes were read out, Jue poured unceasing abuse on the Song. They executed him, packed his head in a box, and delivered it to the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 燕京降將及常勝軍皆泣下，郭藥師自言曰：「若來索藥師當奈何？」

translations.literal: The surrendered generals of Yanjing and the Ever-Victorious Army all wept; Guo Yaoshi said to himself, 'If they come demanding Yaoshi, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing's surrendered generals and the Ever-Victorious Army wept openly. Guo Yaoshi muttered to himself, 'If they come for me next, what then?'

sentences.zh: 自是，降將卒皆解體。

translations.literal: From this time the surrendered generals and soldiers all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment the morale of every surrendered officer and soldier collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及金人伐宋，竟以納平州之叛為執言雲。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens later attacked the Song, they ultimately took sheltering the Ping Prefecture rebel as their stated grievance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens marched against the Song, they ultimately held up the sheltering of the Ping Prefecture rebel as their casus belli.

sentences.zh: 子僅言。

translations.literal: His son Jinyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jinyan.

sentences.zh: 子 僅言

translations.literal: Son: Jinyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jinyan

sentences.zh: 僅言幼名元奴。

translations.literal: Jinyan's childhood name was Yuannu.
translations.idiomatic: As a child Jinyan was called Yuannu.

sentences.zh: 宗望攻下平山，僅言在繈褓間，裏人劉承宣得之，養於家。

translations.literal: When Zongwang captured Pingshan, Jinyan was still in swaddling clothes; a townsman, Liu Chengxuan, took him and raised him in his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang took Pingshan, Jinyan was still an infant. A neighbor, Liu Chengxuan, found him and brought him up in his own home.

sentences.zh: 其鄰韓夫人甚愛之。

translations.literal: A neighbor, Lady Han, loved him dearly.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Han, who lived nearby, adored the child.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，因隨韓夫人得見貞懿皇后。

translations.literal: When he was several years old he accompanied Lady Han and was able to meet Empress Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of a few years he went with Lady Han and was presented to Empress Zhenyi.

sentences.zh: 留之籓邸，稍長，侍世宗讀書，遂使僅言主家事，繩檢部曲，一府憚之。

translations.literal: She kept him at the princely residence; when he grew somewhat older he attended the Shizong Emperor in his studies, and Jinyan was put in charge of household affairs, disciplining the retainers— the whole mansion feared him.
translations.idiomatic: She kept him at the princely residence. As he grew he attended the Shizong Emperor in his studies, then was entrusted with running the household and keeping the retainers in line; the entire establishment stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 僅言能心計，世宗倚任之，凡宮室營造、府庫出納、行幸頓舍皆委之。

translations.literal: Jinyan was skilled in calculation; the Shizong Emperor relied on him, entrusting to him all palace construction, treasury receipts and disbursements, and lodging arrangements on imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan had a sharp head for figures, and the Shizong Emperor leaned on him for palace construction, treasury accounts, and every detail of lodging on the road.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「一經僅言，無不愜朕意者。」

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor once said, 'Once it passes through Jinyan, nothing fails to please my mind.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor once remarked, 'Once Jinyan has handled a matter, it always suits me perfectly.

sentences.zh: 六年，提舉修內役事，役夫掘地得白金匿之，事覺，法當死，僅言責取其物與官，釋其罪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed to oversee inner-palace construction labor; laborers digging earth found white gold and hid it. When the matter came to light the law called for death, but Jinyan compelled them to surrender the goods to the state and released them from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he supervised inner-palace construction. Laborers unearthed hidden silver while digging; when the theft was discovered the law demanded death, but Jinyan made them turn the metal over to the treasury and spared their lives.

sentences.zh: 尋兼祗應司。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also held office in the Attendance Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given additional duties in the Attendance Service.

sentences.zh: 遷少府監，提控宮籍監、祗應司如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Palace Workshop and continued to supervise the Palace Registry and the Attendance Service as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the Palace Workshop while retaining charge of the Palace Registry and the Attendance Service.

sentences.zh: 護作太甯宮，引宮左流泉溉田，歲獲稻萬斛。

translations.literal: He oversaw construction of the Taining Palace, drew the palace's leftward flowing spring to irrigate fields, and harvested ten thousand hu of rice each year.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the Taining Palace he channeled a spring west of the palace to irrigate fields, yielding ten thousand hu of rice a year.

sentences.zh: 十七年，複提點內藏，典領昭德皇后山陵，遷勸農使，領諸職如故。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again supervised the inner treasury, directed the mausoleum of Empress Zhaode, was promoted to Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, and retained his other posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he again oversaw the inner treasury, directed construction of Empress Zhaode's tomb, was made Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, and kept his other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 僅言雖舊臣，出入左右，然世宗終不假以權任。

translations.literal: Although Jinyan was an old retainer who came and went at the emperor's side, the Shizong Emperor never entrusted him with real power.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan was a longtime attendant who moved in the emperor's closest circle, yet the Shizong Emperor never gave him substantive authority.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，尚書省奏，宮苑司直長黎倫在職十六年，請與遷敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Secretariat memorialized that Li Lun, chief clerk of the Palace Parks Office, had served sixteen years and requested promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one the Secretariat reported that Li Lun, chief clerk of the Palace Parks Office, had served sixteen years and asked that his rank be advanced.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此朕之家臣，質直人也，今已老矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'This is a household servant of mine, an honest and straightforward man, and he is old now.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'He is one of my household servants—plain and honest—and he is old now.

sentences.zh: 如勸農使張僅言亦朕舊臣，純實頗解事，凡朝廷議論，內外除授，未嘗得干預。

translations.literal: Likewise Zhang Jinyan, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, is also an old servant of mine—pure, sincere, and quite capable—but in all court deliberations and appointments within and without, he has never been allowed to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinyan, my Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, is another old servant—honest, capable, and thoroughly dependable—yet he has never been permitted to meddle in court debate or in appointments inside or outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 朕觀自古人君為讒諂蒙蔽者多矣，朕雖不及古人，然近習憸言未嘗入耳。」

translations.literal: I observe that since antiquity many rulers have been blinded by slander and flattery; though I do not equal the ancients, sly words from close attendants have never entered my ears.
translations.idiomatic: I know how often ancient rulers were blinded by flatterers and slanderers. I may not match the sages of old, but I have never let the smooth talk of favorites reach my ears.

sentences.zh: 宰臣曰：「誠如聖訓，此國家之福也。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers said, 'Truly as Your Sagely instruction states—this is the fortune of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers replied, 'Your words are wise indeed; such restraint is the state's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲以為橫海軍節度使，而不可去左右，遂止。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor wished to appoint him military commissioner of the Henghai Army, but could not bear to have him leave his side, and so let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor once meant to make him military commissioner of the Henghai Army, but could not part with him from his side, and abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 僅言始得疾，猶扶杖視事，疾亟，詔太醫診視，近侍問訊相屬。

translations.literal: When Jinyan first fell ill he still leaned on his staff to attend to business; when the illness grew critical an edict ordered imperial physicians to examine him, and close attendants came one after another to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyan first fell ill he still leaned on his staff to keep working. As the sickness worsened the court sent imperial physicians, and close attendants called in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上深惜之，遣官致祭，賻銀五百兩、重彩十端、絹二百匹，棺槨、衣衾、銀汞、斂物、葬地皆官給，贈輔國上將軍。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor deeply mourned him, sent officials to offer sacrifice, granted five hundred taels of silver as funeral gifts, ten bolts of heavy-colored silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk; coffin, shroud, silver for the burial rites, grave goods, and burial ground were all provided by the state, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Supporter-of-the-State General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor grieved deeply, sent officials to perform the rites, and granted five hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of fine silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk as funeral gifts. Coffin, shroud, burial silver, grave goods, and burial ground were all supplied by the court, and he was posthumously enfeoffed Supporter-of-the-State General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹

translations.literal: Yelu Yudu
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Yudu

sentences.zh: 太祖已取臨潢府，賜詔余睹曰：「汝將兵在東路，前後戰未嘗不敗。

translations.literal: After the Taizu Emperor had taken Linhuang Prefecture, he granted Yudu an edict saying: 'You command troops on the eastern route and have never won a battle, before or after.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Taizu Emperor had taken Linhuang, he sent Yudu an edict: 'You have led troops on the eastern front and have not won a single battle, time after time.

sentences.zh: 今聞汝收合散亡，以拒我師。

translations.literal: Now I hear you are gathering the scattered and the lost to resist my army.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear you are rallying stragglers and refugees to stand against my army.

sentences.zh: 朕已於今月十五日克上京，今將往取遼主矣。

translations.literal: I have already on the fifteenth of this month taken the Upper Capital; now I am going to seize the Liao ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I captured the Upper Capital on the fifteenth of this month and am now marching to take the Liao emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 汝若治兵一決勝負，可指地期日相報。

translations.literal: If you wish to array your troops and settle victory and defeat in one battle, you may name a place and a date and inform me.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to muster your forces and fight it out, name the place and day and send word.

sentences.zh: 若知不敵，當率眾來降，無貽後悔。」

translations.literal: If you know you cannot match us, you should lead your masses to surrender and not bring regret upon yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: If you know you cannot stand against us, lead your men in submission before regret comes too late.'

sentences.zh: 及太祖班師，闍母等還至遼河，方渡，余睹來襲，完顏背答、烏塔等殿，力戰卻之，獲甲馬五百匹。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor withdrew his army, Chanmu and others returned to the Liao River and were just crossing when Yudu came to attack; Wanyan Beida, Wuta, and others formed the rear guard, fought fiercely and repulsed him, and captured five hundred sets of armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: As the Taizu Emperor marched home, Chanmu and his column reached the Liao River and were mid-crossing when Yudu struck. Wanyan Beida, Wuta, and others held the rear, fought him off after a hard engagement, and seized five hundred sets of armor and mounts.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，余睹送款于咸州路都統，以所部來降，乞援接于桑林渡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, Yudu sent his pledge of submission to the commander-in-chief of the Xianzhou Circuit, came to surrender with his following, and asked to be received at Sanglin Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year five Yudu sent word of submission to the Xianzhou circuit commander, came over with his command, and asked to be met at Sanglin Ford.

sentences.zh: 都統司以聞，詔曰：「余睹到日，使與其官屬偕來，餘眾處之便地。」

translations.literal: The commander's office reported this upward; an edict said: 'On the day Yudu arrives, have him come together with his officials; settle the rest of his people in a suitable place.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's office reported upward, and an edict ordered: 'When Yudu arrives, let him come with his officers; place the rest of his followers wherever is convenient.

sentences.zh: 無何，余睹送上所受遼國宣誥，及器甲旗幟等，與將吏韓福奴、阿八、謝老、太師奴、蕭慶、醜和尚、高佛留、蒲答、謝家奴、五哥等來降。

translations.literal: Before long Yudu presented the Liao imperial commissions he had received, together with weapons, armor, banners, and standards, and came to surrender with his officers Han Funu, Aba, Xielao, Taishinu, Xiao Qing, Chouheshang, Gao Foliu, Puda, Xiejianu, Wuge, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yudu handed over the Liao commissions he had held, along with arms, armor, banners, and standards, and surrendered with his officers Han Funu, Aba, Xielao, Taishinu, Xiao Qing, Chouheshang, Gao Foliu, Puda, Xiejianu, Wuge, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 余睹作書，具言所以降之意，大概以謂：「遼主沉湎荒于遊畋，不恤政事，好佞人，遠忠直，淫刑吝賞，政煩賦重，民不聊生。」

translations.literal: Yudu wrote a letter fully explaining his reasons for surrendering, stating in general that: 'The Liao ruler is sunk in dissipation and waste in hunting, heedless of government affairs, fond of flatterers and distant from the loyal and upright, excessive in punishments and stingy in rewards; government is vexatious and taxes heavy, and the people cannot sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu wrote at length explaining why he had come over. In substance he said: 'The Liao ruler wallows in hunting and pleasure, neglects government, favors sycophants and keeps the loyal at arm's length, punishes harshly yet rewards sparingly; administration is oppressive, taxes crushing, and the people can barely survive.

sentences.zh: 又言：「樞密使得裏底本無材能，但阿諛取容，其子磨哥任以軍事。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'The commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Delidi, has no talent whatsoever but only flatters to win favor; his son Moge is entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'The military commissioner Delidi has no ability at all—he survives by flattery—and his son Moge has been put in charge of the armies.

sentences.zh: 又言：「文妃長子晉王素系人望，宜為儲副，得裏底以元妃諸子己所自出，使晉王出繼文妃。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'The eldest son of Consort Wen, the Prince of Jin, has long commanded popular esteem and ought to be heir apparent; Delidi, because the sons of the primary consort were his own issue, had the Prince of Jin sent out to be adopted to Consort Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The Prince of Jin, eldest son of Consort Wen, has long enjoyed public esteem and should have been made heir; Delidi, wanting the primary consort's sons—his own children—to succeed, had the prince sent out to be adopted to Consort Wen instead.

sentences.zh: 又言：「晉王與駙馬乙信謀複其樞密使，來告余睹共定大計，而所圖不成。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'The Prince of Jin and the imperial son-in-law Yixin plotted to restore him as military commissioner; they came to inform me and together we fixed a great plan, but what we sought did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The Prince of Jin and the imperial son-in-law Yixin plotted to restore his post as military commissioner. They confided in me and we laid a grand design together, but the scheme failed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「己粗更軍事，進策遼主，得裏底蔽之，遼主亦不省察。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'I had myself taken charge of military affairs in rough outline and presented strategies to the Liao ruler, but Delidi concealed them and the Liao ruler likewise did not examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'I had begun to reorganize military affairs and submitted plans to the Liao ruler, but Delidi buried them and the ruler never looked into it.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「大金疆土日辟，余睹灼知天命，遂自去年春與耶律慎思等定議，約以今夏來降。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The Great Jin's territory expands day by day; I clearly perceive Heaven's mandate and therefore, from last spring, fixed plans with Yelu Shensi and others, agreeing to surrender this summer.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The Jin realm grows daily; I see Heaven's mandate clearly. From last spring I agreed with Yelu Shensi and others to come over this summer.

sentences.zh: 近聞得裏底、高十捏等欲發，倉卒之際不及收合四遠，但率傍近部族戶三千、車五千兩、畜產數萬、遼北軍都統以兵追襲，遂棄輜重，轉戰至此。

translations.literal: Recently I heard that Delidi, Gao Shinie, and others intended to move against me; in the emergency I could not gather the distant tribes, but led only the nearby tribal households—three thousand families, five thousand carts, and tens of thousands of livestock. The commander-in-chief of the Northern Liao Army pursued with troops; I therefore abandoned baggage and fought my way here.
translations.idiomatic: I recently learned that Delidi, Gao Shinie, and others meant to strike. In the rush I could not rally distant tribes and brought only three thousand nearby households, five thousand carts, and vast herds. The northern Liao commander pursued with troops, so I abandoned my baggage train and fought my way here.

sentences.zh: 所有官事職位姓名、人戶畜產之數，遣韓福奴具錄以聞。」

translations.literal: The names of all offices and posts, households, and numbers of livestock I have sent Han Funu to record fully and report.
translations.idiomatic: Han Funu will submit a full register of offices, personnel, households, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 遂與其將吏來見，上撫慰之，遂賜坐，班同宰相，賜宴盡醉而罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he came to audience with his officers; the emperor comforted him, granted him a seat, ranked him with the chief ministers, gave a banquet, and dismissed the gathering only when all were thoroughly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He then came to court with his officers. The emperor received him warmly, gave him a seat equal to the chief ministers, feasted him, and sent everyone away only when the wine had done its work.

sentences.zh: 上命余睹以舊官領所部。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yudu to lead his following under his former title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let Yudu command his men under his former rank.

sentences.zh: 且諭之曰：「若能為國立功，別當獎用。」

translations.literal: He also instructed him, saying, 'If you can render merit to the state, you will receive separate reward and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'Serve the state well and you will be rewarded in turn.

sentences.zh: 自余睹降，益知遼人虛實矣。

translations.literal: From Yudu's surrender onward the court came to know ever more clearly the true strength and weakness of the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: After Yudu's defection the court understood the Liao's real condition far better than before.

sentences.zh: 余睹在軍中屢乞侍妾及子，太祖疑之，詔咸州路都統司曰：「余睹家屬，善監護之。」

translations.literal: While in the army Yudu repeatedly asked for concubines and his son; the Taizu Emperor grew suspicious and edicted the Xianzhou Circuit commander's office: 'Yudu's family members are to be well guarded.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Yudu kept asking for concubines and to see his son. The Taizu Emperor grew suspicious and ordered the Xianzhou commander: 'Keep Yudu's family under close watch.

sentences.zh: 複詔曰：「余睹降時，其民多強率而來者，恐在邊生變，宜徙之內地。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: 'When Yudu surrendered, many of his people were forcibly brought along; lest they cause trouble on the frontier, they should be moved to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict added: 'Many of the people who came with Yudu were taken by force. Move them inland before they stir trouble on the border.

sentences.zh: 都統杲取中京，余睹為鄉導，與希尹等招撫奚部。

translations.literal: Commander Gao took the Central Capital; Yudu served as guide and, together with Xiyin and others, pacified and won over the Xi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Gao took the Central Capital, Yudu guided the army and, with Xiyin and others, brought the Xi tribes over by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 奉聖州降，其官吏皆遁去，余睹舉前監酒李師夔為節度使，進士沈璋為副使，州吏裴賾為觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Fengsheng Prefecture surrendered its officials had all fled; Yudu recommended the former wine superintendent Li Shikui as military commissioner, the jinshi Shen Zhang as deputy commissioner, and the prefectural clerk Pei Ze as observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengsheng Prefecture submitted, its officials had fled. Yudu nominated the former wine superintendent Li Shikui as military commissioner, the jinshi Shen Zhang as deputy, and the clerk Pei Ze as observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沈璋招集居民還業者三千餘，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Shen Zhang gathered more than three thousand residents who returned to their occupations and was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhang brought more than three thousand people back to their homes and trades and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久之，耶律麻者告余睹、吳十、劉剌結黨謀叛，及其未發宜先收捕。

translations.literal: After a long while Yelu Mazhe reported that Yudu, Wu Shi, and Liu La had formed a faction to plot rebellion, and that before they acted they ought to be seized first.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Yelu Mazhe accused Yudu, Wu Shi, and Liu La of plotting rebellion together and urged that they be arrested before they could act.

sentences.zh: 上召余睹等從容謂之曰：「今聞汝謀叛，誠然邪，其各無隱。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yudu and the others and said calmly: 'I have now heard that you plot rebellion—is it true? Let each of you hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yudu and the others and said evenly: 'I hear you are plotting rebellion. Is it so? Speak plainly, each of you.

sentences.zh: 若果去，必須鞍馬甲胄器械之屬，當悉付汝，吾不食言。

translations.literal: If you truly mean to go, you will certainly need saddles, horses, armor, weapons, and the like—I will give them all to you; I do not break my word.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to leave, you will need horses, saddles, armor, and arms—I will furnish them all. I do not go back on my word.

sentences.zh: 若再被擒，無祈免死。

translations.literal: If you are captured again, do not hope to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: If you are taken again, do not expect mercy.

sentences.zh: 欲留事我，則無懷異志，吾不汝疑。」

translations.literal: If you wish to remain and serve me, then harbor no other intent—I will not suspect you.
translations.idiomatic: If you choose to stay and serve me, put aside any other design. I will not doubt you.

sentences.zh: 余睹等戰慄不能對，乃杖鐸剌七十，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: Yudu and the others trembled and could not answer; thereupon Duo La was beaten seventy strokes with the staff, and the rest were not questioned further.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu and the rest shook and could not speak. Duo La alone was flogged seventy strokes; the others were let go.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，大舉伐宋，余睹為元帥右都監，宋兵四萬救太原，余睹、屋里海逆擊於汾河北，擒其帥郝仲連、張關索，統制馬忠，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui a great campaign was launched against the Song; Yudu served as right deputy commander-in-chief of the main army. Forty thousand Song troops came to relieve Taiyuan; Yudu and Wulihai counterattacked north of the Fen River, captured their commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Guansuo and the controller Ma Zhong, and killed more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year three the court launched a major invasion of the Song. Yudu was right deputy commander-in-chief. When forty thousand Song troops marched to relieve Taiyuan, Yudu and Wulihai struck them north of the Fen, captured the generals Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Guansuo and the controller Ma Zhong, and killed more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐宋，余睹留西京。

translations.literal: When Zonghan attacked the Song, Yudu remained at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Zonghan campaigned against the Song, Yudu stayed behind at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 天會十年，余睹謀反，雲內節度使耶律奴哥等告之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianhui Yudu plotted rebellion; Yelu Nuge, military commissioner of Yunnei, and others reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year ten Yudu plotted rebellion. Yelu Nuge, military commissioner of Yunnei, and others exposed him.

sentences.zh: 余睹亡去，其黨燕京統軍蕭高六伏誅，蔚州節度使蕭特謀自殺。

translations.literal: Yudu fled; his associate Xiao Gao Liu, commander of Yanjing, was executed, and Xiao Temou, military commissioner of Yu Prefecture, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu fled. His ally Xiao Gao Liu, Yanjing commander, was put to death, and Xiao Temou, military commissioner of Yu Prefecture, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 邊部斬余睹及其諸子，函其首以獻。

translations.literal: Frontier units beheaded Yudu and his sons, boxed their heads, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Border forces hunted him down, killed Yudu and his sons, and sent their heads to court in a box.

sentences.zh: 耶律奴哥加守太保兼侍中，趙公鑒、劉儒信、劉君輔等並授遙鎮節度使以賞之。

translations.literal: Yelu Nuge was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and concurrently Palace Secretary; Zhao Gongjian, Liu Ruxin, Liu Junfu, and others were all appointed titular military commissioners of distant commands as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Nuge was made acting Grand Guardian and Palace Secretary; Zhao Gongjian, Liu Ruxin, Liu Junfu, and the rest received titular frontier military commissions as their reward.

sentences.zh: 移剌窩斡，西北路契丹部族。

translations.literal: Yila Wowa, of the Khitan tribes of the Northwestern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Wowa belonged to the Khitan tribes of the Northwestern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 先從撒八為亂，受其偽署，後殺撒八，遂有其眾。

translations.literal: He had first followed Saba in rebellion, accepted a false appointment from him, later killed Saba, and thereby took over his following.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed Saba's revolt and accepted a post in his rebel regime, then killed Saba and took command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 撒八者，初為招討司譯史。

translations.literal: Saba had originally been an interpreter-clerk in the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Saba had begun as an interpreter in the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 正隆五年，海陵征諸道兵伐宋，使牌印燥合、楊葛盡征西北路契丹丁壯，契丹人曰：「西北路接近鄰國，世世征伐，相為仇怨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenglong the Hailing Emperor levied troops from every circuit to attack the Song and sent the seal-bearer Zaohe and Yang Ge to conscript all able-bodied Khitan men of the Northwestern Circuit. The Khitan said: 'The Northwestern Circuit lies close to neighboring states; generation after generation we have fought wars and borne mutual enmity.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong year five the Hailing Emperor mobilized troops from every circuit for war on the Song and sent Zaohe and Yang Ge to draft every able Khitan man on the Northwestern Circuit. The Khitan protested: 'Our northwestern frontier borders foreign powers; for generations we have fought them and nursed bitter hatred.

sentences.zh: 若男丁盡從軍，彼以兵來，則老弱必盡系累矣。

translations.literal: If all the men are taken into the army and the enemy comes with troops, then the old and the weak will surely all be seized and bound.
translations.idiomatic: If every man is marched away and the enemy strikes, our women, children, and elderly will be carried off without a defender left.

sentences.zh: 幸使者入朝言之。」

translations.literal: We beg the envoy to enter court and report this.
translations.idiomatic: We ask you to carry this plea to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 燥合畏罪不敢言，楊葛深念後西北有事得罪，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: Zaohe, fearing punishment, did not dare speak; Yang Ge brooded deeply that afterward, if trouble arose in the northwest, he would be found guilty, and died of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Zaohe dared not relay their plea for fear of blame. Yang Ge became consumed by the thought that any future trouble in the northwest would fall on him, and died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 燥合複與牌印耶律娜、尚書省令史沒答涅合督起西北路兵。

translations.literal: Zaohe again, together with the seal-bearer Yelü Na and Secretariat clerk Modaniehe, supervised the raising of troops on the Northwestern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zaohe returned with the seal-bearer Yelü Na and Secretariat clerk Modaniehe to press the draft on the Northwestern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 契丹聞男丁當盡起，於是撒八、孛特補與部眾殺招討使完顏沃側及燥合，而執耶律娜、沒答涅合，取招討司貯甲三千，遂反。

translations.literal: When the Khitan heard that all able-bodied men were to be conscripted, Saba, Betebu, and their tribesmen killed Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Woce and Zaohe, seized Yelü Na and Modaniehe, took three thousand suits of armor stored in the Pacification Commission, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that every able man was to be drafted, Saba and Betebu led their followers in killing Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Woce and Zaohe, taking Yelü Na and Modaniehe prisoner and seizing three thousand sets of armor from the commission stores before rising in revolt.

sentences.zh: 議立豫王延禧子孫，眾推都監老和尚為招討使，山后四群牧、山前諸群牧皆應之。

translations.literal: They deliberated on installing a descendant of Prince Yu and Emperor Yanshou, and the multitude proclaimed the commandant Old Monk as Pacification Commissioner; the four horse-pasture offices north of the mountains and all the pasture offices south of the mountains responded.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels debated putting a descendant of Prince Yu on the throne. The crowd raised the commandant known as Old Monk to head the Pacification Commission, and pasture offices on both sides of the mountains joined them.

sentences.zh: 迪斡群牧使徒單賽裏、耶魯瓦群牧使鶴壽等皆遇害，語在《鶴壽傳》中。

translations.literal: Diwo Pasture Commissioner Teshan Saili, Yelüwa Pasture Commissioner Heshou, and others were all killed; the account is given in the Biography of Heshou.
translations.idiomatic: Diwo pasture commissioner Teshan Saili, Yelüwa pasture commissioner Heshou, and others were killed — the story is told in Heshou's biography.

sentences.zh: 五院司部人老和尚那也亦殺節度使術甲兀者以應撒八。

translations.literal: Old Monk Naye, a man of the Wuyuan Department, also killed Military Commissioner Shujiawuzhe to join Saba.
translations.idiomatic: Old Monk Naye of the Wuyuan Department likewise killed Military Commissioner Shujiawuzhe to answer Saba's revolt.

sentences.zh: 會甯八猛安牧馬於山后，至迪謀魯，賊盡奪其馬。

translations.literal: The meng'an chieftain Huiningba was pasturing horses north of the mountains; when he reached Dimolu, the rebels seized all his horses.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an chief Huiningba was grazing horses in the northern hills. At Dimolu the rebels stripped him of every mount.

sentences.zh: 辟沙河千戶十哥等與前招討使完顏麻潑殺烏古迪列招討使烏林答蒲盧虎，以所部趨西北路。

translations.literal: Thousand-household chief Shige of Pisha River and others, together with former Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Mapo, killed Wugudi Pacification Commissioner Ulinad Puluha and marched their following toward the Northwestern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-household chief Shige of Pisha River joined former Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Mapo in killing Ulinad Puluha, Pacification Commissioner of Wugudi, and led their bands toward the northwest.

sentences.zh: 室魯部節度使阿廝列追擊敗之，十哥與數騎遁去，合於撒八。

translations.literal: Shilu Department Military Commissioner Asilie pursued and defeated them; Shige fled with a few horsemen and joined Saba.
translations.idiomatic: Asilie, military commissioner of the Shilu Department, chased them down and routed them. Shige escaped with a handful of riders and threw in with Saba.

sentences.zh: 咸平府謀克括裏，與所部自山后逃歸，咸平少尹完顏餘裏野欲收捕括裏家屬，括裏與其党招誘富家奴隸，數日得眾二千，遂攻陷韓州及柳河縣，遂趨咸平。

translations.literal: Kuoluo, a mouke of Xianping Prefecture, fled back with his following from north of the mountains; Xianping Vice Prefect Wanyan Yuliye wished to seize Kuoluo's family members, and Kuoluo, with his partisans, enticed slaves of wealthy households; within days he gathered two thousand men, captured Han Prefecture and Liuhe County, and then pressed toward Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoluo, a mouke in Xianping Prefecture, slipped back from the northern hills with his men. When Vice Prefect Wanyan Yuliye moved to arrest his family, Kuoluo and his allies recruited slaves from rich households and within days mustered two thousand fighters. They took Han Prefecture and Liuhe County and turned toward Xianping.

sentences.zh: 餘裏野發兵迎擊之，兵敗，賊遂據咸平，於是繕完器甲，出府庫財物以募兵，賊勢益張。

translations.literal: Yuliye sent troops to meet and attack them but was defeated; the rebels then occupied Xianping, repaired weapons and armor, distributed treasury wealth to recruit troops, and rebel strength grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliye marched out to stop them and lost. The rebels held Xianping, refurbished arms and armor, spent the prefectural treasury to recruit men, and their power swelled.

sentences.zh: 權曹家山猛安綽質，集兵千餘，扼幹夜河，賊不得東。

translations.literal: Acting Caojiashan meng'an chieftain Chuozhi gathered more than a thousand soldiers, blocked the Ganye River, and the rebels could not advance east.
translations.idiomatic: Acting meng'an chief Chuozhi of Caojiashan raised a thousand-odd troops and held the Ganye River, barring the rebels from moving east.

sentences.zh: 綽質兵敗，括裏遂犯濟州。

translations.literal: Chuozhi's force was defeated, and Kuoluo then invaded Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chuozhi was beaten, and Kuoluo pushed into Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會宿直將軍孛術魯吳括剌徵兵于速頻路，遇括裏於信州，與猛安烏延查剌兵二千，擊敗括裏。

translations.literal: It happened that Palace Duty General Beshilu Wukuo'a was conscripting troops on the Sufin Route; he encountered Kuoluo at Xin Prefecture and, with meng'an chief Wuyan Chala and two thousand soldiers, defeated Kuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Palace duty general Beshilu Wukuo'a was raising troops on the Sufin Route when he met Kuoluo at Xin Prefecture. With meng'an chief Wuyan Chala and two thousand men he routed the rebel.

sentences.zh: 括裏收余眾趨東京，是時世宗為東京留守，以兵四百人拒之。

translations.literal: Kuoluo gathered his remaining followers and hastened toward the Eastern Capital; at that time the Shizong Emperor was regent of the Eastern Capital and resisted him with four hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoluo regrouped and headed for the Eastern Capital, where the future Shizong Emperor, then regent of Dongjing, met him with four hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 賊至常安縣，聞空中擊鼓聲如數千鼓者，候見旌旗蔽野，傳言留守以十萬兵至矣，即引還，亦以其眾合於撒八。

translations.literal: When the rebels reached Chang'an County they heard in the air the sound of drumming as if from thousands of drums; they looked and saw banners covering the plain, and it was rumored that the regent had arrived with a hundred thousand soldiers — they at once withdrew and also united their followers with Saba.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an County the rebels heard what sounded like thousands of drums in the empty air and saw banners blot out the fields. Word spread that the regent had come with a hundred thousand men — they pulled back at once and rejoined Saba.

sentences.zh: 海陵使樞密使僕散忽土、西京留守蕭懷忠將兵一萬，與右衛將軍蕭禿剌討平之。

translations.literal: The Hailing Emperor sent Privy Council Commissioner Pusan Hutu and Western Capital Regent Xiao Huaizhong with ten thousand troops, together with Right Guard General Xiao Tula, to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing dispatched Privy Council Commissioner Pusan Hutu and Western Capital regent Xiao Huaizhong with ten thousand men, joined by Right Guard General Xiao Tula, to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 禿剌與之相持數日，連與戰皆無功，而糧餉不繼，禿剌退歸臨潢。

translations.literal: Tula faced them for several days; he fought repeatedly without success, and as grain supplies failed to keep up, Tula withdrew and returned to Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Tula locked with the rebels for days and fought again and again without result. Supplies ran dry, and he fell back to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 禿剌雖不能克敵，而撒八自度大軍必相繼而至，勢不可支，謀歸於大石，乃率眾沿龍駒河西出。

translations.literal: Although Tula could not overcome the enemy, Saba reckoned that great armies would surely come in succession and that his position could not be held; he planned to submit to Dashi and therefore led his following west along the Longju River.
translations.idiomatic: Tula had failed to break them, but Saba judged that imperial armies would keep coming and that he could not hold out. He meant to join Dashi and led his people west along the Longju River.

sentences.zh: 及僕散忽土、蕭懷忠等兵至，與禿剌合兵追至河上，不及而還。

translations.literal: When Pusan Hutu, Xiao Huaizhong, and the others arrived with their troops and joined Tula in pursuit to the river, they could not overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Pusan Hutu and Xiao Huaizhong arrived and combined with Tula, they chased the rebels to the river but could not catch them and turned back.

sentences.zh: 忽土、懷忠、禿剌坐逗遛不即追賊，皆誅死。

translations.literal: Hutu, Huaizhong, and Tula were punished for delaying and not pursuing the rebels promptly; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu, Huaizhong, and Tula were condemned for their sluggish pursuit and put to death.

sentences.zh: 北京留守蕭賾不能制其下，殺降人而取其婦女，亦坐誅。

translations.literal: Northern Capital Regent Xiao Ze could not control his subordinates; they killed surrendered persons and took their women — he too was executed for this.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Capital regent Xiao Ze lost control of his men, who slaughtered surrendering Khitan and seized their women. He was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 於是，白彥恭為北面兵馬都統，紇石烈志寧副之，守顏彀英為西北面兵馬都統，西北路招討使唐括孛姑的副之，以討撒八等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bai Yangong was made Northern Route Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry and Infantry, with Heshilie Zhining as his deputy; Wanyan Guyin was made Northwestern Route Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry and Infantry, with Northwestern Circuit Pacification Commissioner Tangqut Ligude as deputy — to campaign against Saba and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yangong was appointed northern commander-in-chief with Heshilie Zhining as his deputy; Wanyan Guyin took the northwestern command with Tangqut Ligude, Pacification Commissioner of the Northwestern Circuit, as second — all to suppress Saba and his allies.

sentences.zh: 撒八既西行，而舊居山前者皆不欲往，偽署六院節度使移刺窩斡、兵官陳家殺撒八，執老和尚、孛特補等。

translations.literal: After Saba had marched west, those who had formerly lived south of the mountains all did not wish to go; the falsely appointed Six-District Military Commissioner Yila Wowa and military officer Chen Jia killed Saba and seized Old Monk, Betebu, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Once Saba marched west, his followers from south of the mountains refused to follow. Yila Wowa, their self-appointed commissioner of the Six Districts, and military officer Chen Jia killed Saba and took Old Monk, Betebu, and the rest prisoner.

sentences.zh: 至是，窩斡始自為都元帥，陳家為都監，擁眾東還，至臨潢府東南新羅寨。

translations.literal: At this point Wowa first made himself supreme commander, with Chen Jia as chief overseer, and led his following east, reaching Xinluo Stockade southeast of Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa then proclaimed himself supreme commander, made Chen Jia his chief overseer, and marched east with his host to Xinluo Stockade, southeast of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 世宗使移剌紮八、前押軍謀克播斡、前牌印麻駭、利涉軍節度判官馬腦等招之。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor sent Yila Zhaba, former Escort Army mouke Bowo, former seal-bearer Mahai, Lieshe Army military commissioner's aide Manao, and others to summon them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong dispatched Yila Zhaba, former escort mouke Bowo, former seal-bearer Mahai, and Lieshe Army commissioner aide Manao to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 紮八等見窩斡，以上意諭之。

translations.literal: Zhaba and the others saw Wowa and conveyed the emperor's intent to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba and his party met Wowa and delivered the emperor's message.

sentences.zh: 窩斡已約降，已而複謂紮八曰：「若降，爾能保我輩無事乎？」

translations.literal: Wowa had already agreed to surrender; then he again said to Zhaba: 'If we surrender, can you guarantee that we will come to no harm?
translations.idiomatic: Wowa had already pledged to yield, but then he asked Zhaba, 'If we submit, can you guarantee we will not be punished?

sentences.zh: 紮八曰：「我知招降耳，其他豈能必哉。」

translations.literal: Zhaba said: 'I know only how to summon surrender; how could I guarantee anything beyond that?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba replied, 'My charge is to offer surrender — I cannot promise anything more than that.'

sentences.zh: 紮八見窩斡兵眾強，車帳滿野，意其可以有成，因說之曰：「我之始來，以汝輩不能有為，今觀兵勢強盛如此，汝等欲如群羊為人所驅去乎，將欲待天時乎？

translations.literal: Zhaba saw that Wowa's troops were strong and carts and tents filled the plain; he thought success was possible, and therefore urged him: 'When I first came, I thought you could accomplish nothing; now I see your military strength so great — do you wish to be like a flock of sheep driven off by others, or wait for Heaven's season?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wowa's forces strong and tents stretching across the plain, Zhaba decided they might yet prevail and pressed him: 'When I arrived I thought you had no future. Look at this army — will you let yourselves be driven like sheep, or seize the moment Heaven has given you?

sentences.zh: 若果有大志，吾亦不復還矣。」

translations.literal: If you truly have great ambition, I too will not return.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to fight on, I will stay with you and not go back.

sentences.zh: 賊將有前孛特本部族節度使逐斡者，言：「昔谷神丞相，賢能人也，嘗說他日西北部族當有事。

translations.literal: Among the rebel generals was Zhuwo, former Betebu tribal military commissioner, who said: 'Formerly Chancellor Gushen, a man of talent and ability, once said that someday the northwestern tribes would have trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Zhuwo, once tribal commissioner of the Betebu department, spoke up: 'Chancellor Gushen, a wise man, once prophesied that the northwestern tribes would one day rise.

sentences.zh: 今日正合此語，恐不可降也。」

translations.literal: Today exactly fits those words — I fear we must not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That day has come. I do not believe we should surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是，窩斡遂決意不復肯降矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wowa resolved at last that he would no longer consent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At that Wowa made up his mind not to yield after all.

sentences.zh: 紮八亦留賊中，惟麻駭、播斡還歸。

translations.literal: Zhaba also remained among the rebels; only Mahai and Bowo returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba stayed with the rebels; only Mahai and Bowo came back.

sentences.zh: 窩斡乃引兵攻臨潢府，總管移室懣出城戰，兵少被執，賊遂圍臨潢，眾至五萬。

translations.literal: Wowa then led troops to attack Linhuang Prefecture; Administrator Yishi Man went out to fight but, with few soldiers, was captured; the rebels then besieged Linhuang, their numbers reaching fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa marched on Linhuang. Prefect Yishi Man rode out with too few men, was taken prisoner, and the rebels invested the city with a force of fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年十二月己亥，窩斡遂稱帝，改元天正。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhenglong, Wowa declared himself emperor and changed the era name to Tianzheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, twelfth month, Zhenglong 6, Wowa proclaimed himself emperor and adopted the era name Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，北面都統白彥敬、副統紇石烈志寧在北京，聞世宗即位，以兵來歸。

translations.literal: At this time Northern Supreme Commander Bai Yanjing and Deputy Supreme Commander Heshilie Zhining were at Beijing; hearing that Shizong had ascended the throne, they came with their troops to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Northern supreme commander Bai Yanjing and his deputy Heshilie Zhining were at Beijing. When they learned Shizong had taken the throne, they marched their armies to his side.

sentences.zh: 世宗使元帥左都監吾紮忽、同知北京留守事完顏骨只救臨潢，晝夜兼行，比至臨潢，賊已解圍去攻泰州。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor sent Left Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief Wuzhahu and Co-Regent of the Northern Capital Wanyan Guzhi to rescue Linhuang; they marched day and night without rest, but by the time they reached Linhuang the rebels had lifted the siege and gone to attack Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent left army supervisor Wuzhahu and co-regent of Beijing Wanyan Guzhi to relieve Linhuang. They forced the march day and night, but when they arrived the rebels had already broken off the siege and were striking at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽追及於窊曆，兩軍已陣將戰，押軍猛安契丹忽剌叔以所部兵應賊，吾紮忽軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Wuzhahu overtook them at Wali; both armies had already formed ranks and were about to fight when the Khitan escort meng'an Hulashu supported the rebels with his command — Wuzhahu's army was then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhahu caught them at Wali just as both sides were forming for battle. Escort meng'an Hulashu, a Khitan, went over to the rebels with his unit, and Wuzhahu's force was routed.

sentences.zh: 泰州節度使烏裏雅率千餘騎與窩斡遇，烏裏雅兵複敗，僅以數騎脫歸。

translations.literal: Taizhou Military Commissioner Wuliya led more than a thousand horsemen and encountered Wowa; Wuliya's force was again defeated, and he escaped home with only a few riders.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou commissioner Wuliya met Wowa with a thousand horsemen, was beaten again, and got back with only a handful of mounts.

sentences.zh: 賊勢愈振，城中震駭，莫敢出戰。

translations.literal: Rebel strength grew ever bolder; the city was shaken with terror, and no one dared go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel momentum surged. Terror gripped the city, and no one would sally out.

sentences.zh: 賊四面登城，押軍猛安烏古孫阿裏補率軍士數人，各持刀以身率先循城擊賊力戰，斫刈甚眾，賊乃退走，城賴以完。

translations.literal: The rebels climbed the walls on all four sides. Escort meng'an Wugusun Alibu led several soldiers, each holding a blade and taking the lead in person along the wall to strike the rebels and fight fiercely; he cut down very many, and the rebels then withdrew — the city was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels scaled the walls from every side. Escort meng'an Wugusun Alibu led a few soldiers along the ramparts, blades in hand, cutting down rebels in the forefront of the fight until the assault broke — and the city held.

sentences.zh: 泰州司吏顏盞蒲查奏捷，除忠翊校尉，賜銀五十兩、重彩十端。

translations.literal: Taizhou clerk Yanzhan Pucha reported the victory; he was appointed Loyal Assistant Commandant and granted fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Yanzhan Pucha brought word of the victory. He was made Loyal Assistant Commandant and given fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，右副元帥完顏謀衍率諸軍北征窩斡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Mouyan led the various armies north to campaign against Wowa.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two, right deputy commander Wanyan Mouyan led the armies north against Wowa.

sentences.zh: 二月壬戌詔曰：「應諸人若能於契丹賊中自拔歸者，更不問元初首從及被威脅之由，奴婢、良人罪無輕重並行免放。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the second month an edict said: 'All persons who can extricate themselves from among the Khitan rebels and return — no further inquiry shall be made into whether they were original ringleaders or had been coerced; bond servants and commoners, guilt heavy or light alike, shall all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, second month, an edict declared: 'Anyone who breaks away from the Khitan rebels and returns will not be questioned about original leadership or coercion. Bond servants and freemen alike, whatever their offense, shall be fully pardoned.

sentences.zh: 曾有官職及糾率人眾來歸者，仍與官賞，依本品量材敘使。

translations.literal: Those who once held office and those who rallied people to return shall still receive official rewards and appointments suited to their original ranks according to their talent.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials and those who bring followers back will still receive offices and rewards, appointed according to their former rank and ability.

sentences.zh: 其同來人各從所願處收系，有才能者亦與錄用。

translations.literal: Those who come together with them may each be registered wherever they wish; those with ability shall also be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who come with them may settle wherever they choose; capable men among them will also be given posts.

sentences.zh: 內外官員郎君群牧直撒百姓人家驅奴、宮籍監人等，並放為良，亦從所願處收系，與免三年差役。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials, langjun, pasture-office clerks, commoners' driven slaves, palace-registry slaves, and the like shall all be freed as commoners; they may also be registered wherever they wish and shall receive exemption from corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' dependents, pasture clerks, household slaves, palace-registry slaves — all are to be made freemen, registered where they wish, and exempt from labor levies for three years.

sentences.zh: 或能捕殺首領而歸者，准上施行，仍驗勞績約量遷賞。

translations.literal: If any can capture or kill rebel leaders and return, the above provisions shall apply, and according to merit they shall receive measured advancement and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Those who capture or kill rebel leaders shall receive the same benefits, with promotion scaled to their merit.

sentences.zh: 如捕獲窩斡者，猛安加三品官授節度使，謀克加四品官授防禦使，庶人加五品官授刺史。」

translations.literal: If Wowa is captured, a meng'an shall be raised three ranks and made military commissioner; a mouke raised four ranks and made defense commissioner; a commoner raised five ranks and made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever captures Wowa will receive: for a meng'an, promotion by three ranks to military commissioner; for a mouke, four ranks to defense commissioner; for a commoner, five ranks to prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「尚書省，如節度防禦使捉獲窩斡者與世襲猛安，刺史捉獲者與世襲謀克，驅奴、宮籍監人亦與庶人同。」

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Imperial Secretariat — if a military or defense commissioner captures Wowa, grant a hereditary meng'an; if a prefect captures him, grant a hereditary mouke; driven slaves and palace-registry slaves receive the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict to the Secretariat: military and defense commissioners who capture Wowa receive a hereditary meng'an; prefects receive a hereditary mouke; slaves and palace-registry bondservants are treated as commoners.

sentences.zh: 複詔宰臣，遍諭將士，能捕殺窩斡者加特進、授真總管。

translations.literal: Another edict to the chief ministers directed that the troops be told throughout: whoever captures or kills Wowa shall receive extraordinary advancement and be appointed true supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were also ordered to proclaim to every soldier: whoever kills or captures Wowa will be raised to extraordinary advancement and made supreme commander in full.

sentences.zh: 於是，括裏將犯韓州，聞元帥兵至，不戰遁去，將轉趨懿、宜州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kuoluo was about to invade Han Prefecture; hearing that the commander's army had arrived, he fled without fighting and was about to turn toward Yi and Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoluo was heading for Han Prefecture when he heard the commander's army was near. He slipped away without a fight and turned toward Yi and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 謀衍屯懿州慶雲縣，及屯川州武平縣，奏請糧運當遣人護送，兵仗乞選精良者付之。

translations.literal: Mouyan encamped at Qingyun County in Yi Prefecture and at Wuping County in Chuan Prefecture; he memorialized that grain transport should be sent with escorts and requested that choice weapons be issued to them.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan camped at Qingyun in Yi Prefecture and Wuping in Chuan Prefecture. He asked that supply convoys be escorted and that the best arms be issued to the guards.

sentences.zh: 詔以南征逃還軍士就往屯戍，如不足，量于富家簽調，就近地簽步軍，給仗護送糧運。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that soldiers who had fled back from the southern campaign be sent directly to garrison duty; if insufficient, men were to be conscripted from wealthy households as needed, and infantry conscripted locally nearby, given weapons to escort grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed deserters from the southern campaign to garrison duty. If numbers fell short, wealthy households were to supply men, local infantry were to be drafted nearby, armed and assigned to escort the grain.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事移剌元宜往泰州規措邊事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Councilor Yila Yuanyi to go to Taizhou to arrange border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilor Yila Yuanyi was ordered to Taizhou to manage frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 前安遠大將軍斡裏嫋、猛安七斤、庶人阿裏葛、磨哥等自窩斡中來降，斡裏嫋、七斤加昭武大將軍，阿裏葛武義將軍，磨哥忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: Former Pacification Grand General Woli Niao, meng'an Qijin, commoners Alige and Moge, and others came to surrender from among Wowa's forces; Woli Niao and Qijin were promoted to Illustrious Martial Grand Generals, Alige to Martial Righteousness General, and Moge to Loyal Valor Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Former pacification grand general Woli Niao, meng'an Qijin, and commoners Alige and Moge defected from Wowa's camp. Woli Niao and Qijin were made Illustrious Martial Grand Generals; Alige became Martial Righteousness General; Moge, Loyal Valor Commandant.

sentences.zh: 窩斡遂自泰州往攻濟州，欲邀糧運。

translations.literal: Wowa then marched from Taizhou to attack Ji Prefecture, intending to intercept grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa left Taizhou to strike at Ji Prefecture, hoping to cut off the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 元帥完顏謀衍與右監軍完顏福壽、左都監吾紮忽合兵，甲士萬三千人，曷懶路總管徒單克甯、廣甯尹僕散渾坦、同知廣甯尹完顏岩雅、肇州防禦使唐括烏也為左翼，臨海節度使紇石烈志寧、曷速館節度使神土懣、同知北京留守完顏骨只、淄州刺史尼龐古鈔兀為右翼，至術虎崖，盡委輜重，士卒齎數日糧，輕騎襲之。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Mouyan joined forces with Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Fushou and Left Army Supervisor Wuzhahu, with thirteen thousand armored soldiers; Yilan Route Administrator Teshan Kening, Guangning Prefect Pusan Huntan, Co-Prefect of Guangning Wanyan Yanya, and Zhaozhou Defense Commissioner Tangqut Wuye formed the left wing; Linhai Military Commissioner Heshilie Zhining, Yisuguan Military Commissioner Shentu Man, Co-Regent of the Northern Capital Wanyan Guzhi, and Zizhou Prefect Nipanggu Chaowu formed the right wing; they reached Shuhuya, left all baggage behind, had the soldiers carry several days' grain, and made a light-cavalry raid.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wanyan Mouyan combined with right supervisor Wanyan Fushou and left supervisor Wuzhahu — thirteen thousand armored men in all. Teshan Kening, Pusan Huntan, Wanyan Yanya, and Tangqut Wuye led the left; Heshilie Zhining, Shentu Man, Wanyan Guzhi, and Nipanggu Chaowu the right. At Shuhuya they stripped away all baggage, gave each man a few days' rations, and swept in with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 糺椀群牧人契丹颭者，與其弟孛迭、挼剌，皆棄家自賊中來降。

translations.literal: Jiu, a Khitan of the Jiuwan Pasture Office, together with his younger brothers Beidie and Ruola, all abandoned their families and came to surrender from among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu, a Khitan of the Jiuwan pasture office, and his brothers Beidie and Ruola all deserted their homes and defected from the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 糺者謂謀衍曰：「賊中馬肥健，官軍馬疲弱，此去賊八十里，比遇賊馬已憊。

translations.literal: Jiu said to Mouyan: 'The rebels' horses are fat and strong; the government army's horses are weak and exhausted. The rebels are eighty li from here — by the time we meet them their horses will already be weary.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu told Mouyan, 'The rebels' mounts are fresh and strong; ours are spent. They are eighty li away — by the time we reach them their horses will be tired.

sentences.zh: 賊輜重去此不遠，我攻之，賊必救其巢穴，賊至馬必疲，我馬少得息，所謂攻其所必救，以逸待勞者也。」

translations.literal: The rebels' baggage is not far from here; if we attack it, the rebels will surely rescue their nest — when they arrive their horses will be exhausted and our horses will have had a little rest; this is what is called attacking what they must rescue and awaiting the weary with the rested.
translations.idiomatic: Their baggage train is close by. Strike it and they must come to its defense — their horses will be blown, ours will have caught breath. That is the classic move: hit what they cannot abandon and meet fatigue with fresh strength.

sentences.zh: 謀衍從之，乘夜亟發，會大風路暗不能辨，遲明行三十里許，與賊輜重相近，整兵少憩。

translations.literal: Mouyan followed this advice and set out urgently by night; they encountered a great wind and the road was dark and hard to discern; at daybreak they had marched about thirty li and were near the rebels' baggage — they formed ranks and rested briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan took his counsel and marched hard through the night. A gale blotted out the road; at first light they had covered some thirty li and were near the rebel baggage. They formed up and rested briefly.

sentences.zh: 窩斡趨濟州，知大軍取其輜重，乃還救，遇於長濼。

translations.literal: Wowa pressed toward Ji Prefecture; learning that the great army was seizing his baggage, he turned back to rescue it and met them at Chang Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa was hurrying toward Ji Prefecture when he learned the imperial army had seized his baggage. He swung back to save it and met them at Chang Marsh.

sentences.zh: 既陣，謀衍別設伏於左翼之側，賊四百餘騎突出左翼伏兵之間，徒單克寧射卻之。

translations.literal: Once ranks were formed, Mouyan set an ambush separately on the flank of the left wing; more than four hundred rebel horsemen burst out between the left-wing ambushers, and Teshan Kening shot them back.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies formed, Mouyan hid troops on the left flank. Four hundred rebel riders burst through the gap; Teshan Kening drove them off with arrows.

sentences.zh: 是日，別部諸將與賊對者，勝負未分，相去五里許而立。

translations.literal: That day the various generals of the separate divisions facing the rebels had not yet decided victory or defeat and stood about five li apart.
translations.idiomatic: That day the detached commanders facing the rebels were still locked in stalemate, their lines some five li apart.

sentences.zh: 左翼萬戶襄別與賊戰，賊陣動，襄麾軍乘之，突出其後，俱與大軍不相及。

translations.literal: Left-wing commander of ten thousand households Xiangbie fought the rebels; the rebel formation shifted, Xiang waved his army forward and seized the moment, bursting out behind them — all became cut off from the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Left-wing commander Xiangbie engaged the rebels. When their line wavered he pressed the attack, swung behind them, and was cut off from the main force.

sentences.zh: 襄以善射者二十騎，率眾自賊後擊之，賊不能支，乘勢麾軍擊其一偏，賊遂卻。

translations.literal: Xiang, with twenty skilled archers on horseback, led his followers to strike the rebels from behind; the rebels could not hold, and seizing the momentum he waved his army to attack one flank — the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang took twenty crack archers and hit the rebels from the rear. They buckled; he pressed one flank and the enemy gave ground.

sentences.zh: 襄遂與大軍合，而別部諸將皆至，整陣力戰，忽反風揚砂石，賊陣亂，官軍馳擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiang then rejoined the main army, and the generals of the separate divisions all arrived; they formed ranks and fought fiercely — suddenly the wind reversed and blew sand and stones, the rebel formation fell into disorder, and the government army charged and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang rejoined the main army as the detached commanders came up. They formed and fought hard; then the wind shifted, sand and gravel flew into the rebel ranks, and the imperial cavalry charged home for a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 追北十餘裏，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: They pursued the fleeing enemy more than ten li and killed and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than ten li; the slaughter and captures were immense.

sentences.zh: 詔以糺者為武義將軍，孛迭昭信校尉，挼剌忠翊校尉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jiu as Martial Righteousness General, Beidie as Bright Trust Commandant, and Ruola as Loyal Assistant Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu was made Martial Righteousness General; Beidie, Bright Trust Commandant; Ruola, Loyal Assistant Commandant.

sentences.zh: 糺除同知建州事，未之官，卒。

translations.literal: Jiu was appointed Co-Administrator of Jian Prefecture but did not take up the post and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu was named co-administrator of Jian Prefecture but died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 孛迭取家賊中，遂被害，上憫之，後以挼剌為汝州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Beidie went to fetch his family from among the rebels and was thereupon killed; the emperor pitied him, and afterward Ruola was made Chief Inspector of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Beidie went back into rebel territory to bring out his family and was killed. The emperor mourned him, and later made Ruola chief inspector of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 窩斡率其眾西走，謀衍追及之於霿𩃭河。

translations.literal: Wowa led his following west in flight, and Mouyan overtook him at the Mengjing River.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa fled west with his host, and Mouyan caught him at the Mengjing River.

sentences.zh: 賊已濟，毀其津口，紇石烈志寧軍先至，不克渡，乃對岸為疑兵，以夾穀清臣、徒單海羅兩萬戶於下流渡河，值支港兩岸鬥絕且濘淖，命軍士束柳填港而過。

translations.literal: The rebels had already crossed and destroyed the ford; Heshilie Zhining's army arrived first but could not cross, so he made a feint on the opposite bank and had the two commanders of ten thousand households Jiagu Qingchen and Teshan Hailuo cross downstream; they came to a branch channel whose banks were steep cliffs and mire, and he ordered the soldiers to bundle willows to fill the channel and pass over.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had crossed and wrecked the ford. Heshilie Zhining arrived first but could not get over; he feinted on the far bank while Jiagu Qingchen and Teshan Hailuo forded downstream. At a side channel with sheer banks and mud they had the men pack willow bundles into the mire and cross.

sentences.zh: 追之數裏，得平地，方食，賊眾奄至。

translations.literal: After pursuing several li they reached level ground and were just eating when the rebel host suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: They chased several li to open ground and had just begun to eat when the rebels fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 志寧軍急整陣，賊自南岡馳下，沖陣者三，志寧力戰，流矢中左臂，戰自若。

translations.literal: Zhining's army hurriedly formed ranks; the rebels charged down from the southern ridge and broke the formation three times; Zhining fought fiercely, was struck in the left arm by a stray arrow, and fought on as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining's men scrambled into formation as the rebels swept down from the southern ridge and broke their line three times. An arrow struck Zhining's left arm; he fought on without flinching.

sentences.zh: 大軍畢至，左翼騎兵先與賊接，賊據上風縱火，乘煙擊官軍，官軍步兵亦至，並力合戰，凡十余合，軍士苦風煙皆植立如癡。

translations.literal: The main army all arrived; the left-wing cavalry engaged the rebels first; the rebels held the upwind position and set fires, striking the government army through the smoke; government infantry also arrived, and all joined in battle — more than ten engagements in all; the soldiers, tormented by wind and smoke, stood rooted like men in a daze.
translations.idiomatic: The main force came up; left-wing cavalry met the rebels first. The rebels held the windward side, set fires, and struck through the smoke. Infantry joined in; the fight ran through more than ten clashes. Choked by wind and smoke, the soldiers stood frozen as if stunned.

sentences.zh: 會天降雨，風止，官軍奮擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Then Heaven sent rain, the wind stopped, and the government army charged fiercely and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell, the wind died, and the imperial troops surged forward for a decisive rout.

sentences.zh: 徒單克寧追奔十五里，賊前厄溪澗不得亟渡，多殺傷。

translations.literal: Teshan Kening pursued the fleeing enemy fifteen li; the rebels were blocked ahead by streams and ravines and could not cross quickly — many were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Teshan Kening chased them fifteen li. Streams and gullies blocked the rebels' path; many were cut down before they could cross.

sentences.zh: 賊既渡，官軍亦渡，少憩，賊反旆來攻，克甯以大軍不繼，令軍士皆下馬射賊。

translations.literal: After the rebels had crossed, the government army also crossed and rested briefly; the rebels turned their banners and came to attack; Kening, because the main army had not followed up, ordered the soldiers all to dismount and shoot at the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels were across, the imperial troops crossed too and paused. The rebels wheeled about and attacked. With the main force not yet up, Kening had his men dismount and shoot.

sentences.zh: 賊引卻而南，克寧亦將引而北，士未及騎馬，賊複來衝突，官軍少卻，回渡澗北。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew southward; Kening was also about to withdraw northward — the soldiers had not yet remounted when the rebels again charged; the government army fell back slightly and recrossed to the north of the stream.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pulled back south; Kening meant to withdraw north. Before his men could remount the rebels charged again. The imperial line gave ground and recrossed to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 大軍至，賊遂引去。

translations.literal: When the main army arrived, the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force came up, the rebels broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔元帥府曰；

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict to the Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the court addressed the commander-in-chief's headquarters:

sentences.zh: 「應契丹賊人，與大兵未戰已前投降者，不得殺傷，仍加安撫。

translations.literal: 'All Khitan rebels who surrender before engaging the main army must not be killed or harmed, and shall receive reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: 'Khitan rebels who surrender before battle must not be harmed and shall be treated with leniency.

sentences.zh: 敗走以後，招誘來降者，除奴婢准已虜為定外，親屬分付圓聚。

translations.literal: Those who come to surrender after defeat, having been enticed, shall — apart from bond servants, who shall be counted according to those already captured — have their kin assigned to gather together.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrender after defeat shall have their families reunited; bond servants already taken captive are excepted.

sentences.zh: 仍官為換贖。」

translations.literal: The government shall also redeem them on their behalf.'
translations.idiomatic: The state will also redeem them at public expense.'

sentences.zh: 窩斡既敗，謀衍不復追討，駐軍白濼。

translations.literal: After Wowa was defeated, Mouyan did not pursue further but encamped at Bai Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: After Wowa's defeat Mouyan stopped the pursuit and camped at Bai Marsh.

sentences.zh: 窩斡攻懿州不克，遂殘破川州，將遁於山西，而北京亦不邀擊之。

translations.literal: Wowa attacked Yi Prefecture without success, then ravaged Chuan Prefecture and was about to flee into western Shanxi, yet Beijing also did not intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa failed to take Yi Prefecture, laid waste to Chuan Prefecture, and was slipping toward western Shanxi — yet Beijing never moved to block him.

sentences.zh: 於是，發驍騎軍二千、曷懶路留屯京師軍三千，號稱二萬，會寧濟州軍六千亦號二萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon two thousand elite cavalry were mobilized and three thousand Yilan Route troops garrisoned at the capital were called up, proclaimed as twenty thousand; six thousand Huining and Ji Prefecture troops were also proclaimed as twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand elite cavalry were called out, plus three thousand Yilan troops from the capital garrison — billed as twenty thousand. Six thousand from Huining and Ji Prefecture were likewise counted as twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 元帥左都監高忠建總兵，沃州刺史烏古論蒲查為曷懶路押軍萬戶，祁州刺史烏林答剌撒為濟州押軍萬戶，右驍騎副都指揮使烏延查剌為驍騎萬戶，祁州刺史宗甯為會甯路押軍萬戶，右宣徽使宗亨為北京路都統，吏部郎中完顏達吉為副統，會元帥府討擊之。
