translations.literal: Left Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief Gao Zhongjian took overall command; Wo Prefecture Prefect Wugulun Pucha was made Yilan Route escort commander of ten thousand households; Qi Prefecture Prefect Ulinad Lasa was made Ji Prefecture escort commander of ten thousand households; Right Elite Cavalry Deputy Commander Wuyan Chala was made elite cavalry commander of ten thousand households; Qi Prefecture Prefect Zongning was made Huining Route escort commander of ten thousand households; Right Palace Attendant Intendant Zongheng was made Northern Capital Route supreme commander, and Ministry of Personnel Director Wanyan Daji was deputy supreme commander — they joined the Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Left army supervisor Gao Zhongjian took overall command. Wugulun Pucha of Wo Prefecture led the Yilan escort force; Ulinad Lasa of Qi Prefecture the Ji escort; Wuyan Chala, deputy commander of elite cavalry, the cavalry wing; Zongning of Qi Prefecture the Huining escort. Right palace intendant Zongheng commanded the Beijing route with Wanyan Daji of the Ministry of Personnel as his deputy. They joined headquarters to hunt the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 詔使尚廄局副使蒲察蒲盧渾往懿州戒敕將帥，上曰：「朕委卿等討賊，乃聞不就賊趨戰，而駐兵閑緩，經涉累月，雖曾追襲，乃不由有水草之地，以致馬疲弱不能百里而還。

translations.literal: An edict sent Deputy Director of the Imperial Stud Bureau Pucha Puluhun to Yi Prefecture to admonish the generals; the emperor said: 'I entrusted you with suppressing the rebels, yet I hear you did not press toward the enemy to fight but encamped at leisure for months on end; although you once pursued, you did not go by places with water and pasture, so that the horses grew weak and exhausted and could not return after a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy director of the Imperial Stud Bureau Pucha Puluhun was sent to Yi Prefecture to rebuke the commanders. The emperor said, 'I charged you with destroying these rebels, yet you linger in camp instead of closing with the enemy — for months. When you did pursue, you avoided watered pasture; your horses broke down and could not even run a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 後雖破賊，而縱諸軍劫掠，數日後方追北霿𩃭河，亦不乘勝，輒複引還。

translations.literal: Later, although you defeated the rebels, you let the armies plunder freely; only after several days did you pursue north to the Mengjing River, and even then you did not press the victory but again withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Even after you beat them you let the troops loot at will. Days passed before you chased them to the Mengjing River — and then you failed to press the advantage and pulled back again.

sentences.zh: 賊遂入涉近地，北京、懿州由此受兵。

translations.literal: The rebels then entered and raided nearby territory; Beijing and Yi Prefecture thereby suffered attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped into the settled districts; Beijing and Yi Prefecture bore the brunt of their raids.

sentences.zh: 朕欲重譴汝等，以方任兵事，且圖後功。

translations.literal: I wish to punish you severely, but since you are still entrusted with military affairs, I shall look for merit hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to punish you severely, but you are still in command — I will look for better work from you hereafter.

sentences.zh: 當盡心一力，毋得似前怠弛。」

translations.literal: You must devote your full effort and must not be slack as before.
translations.idiomatic: Give your full effort. There must be no repeat of such slackness.

sentences.zh: 上謂蒲盧渾曰：「卿若聞賊在近，即當監督討伐。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Puluhun: 'If you hear the rebels are near, you must at once supervise the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Puluhun, 'When you hear the rebels are close, you must ride out and oversee the fighting.

sentences.zh: 用命力戰者疏記以聞，朕將約量遷賞。

translations.literal: Those who obey orders and fight fiercely — record them in memorial and report; I shall measure their merit and grant advancement and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Record every man who fights hard and obey orders; I will weigh their merit and promote them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 無或承徇上官，抑有功、濫署無功者。

translations.literal: None may indulge their superiors, suppress the meritorious, or indiscriminately register the unmeritorious.
translations.idiomatic: No one is to curry favor with superiors, pass over men who have earned credit, or put unearned names on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 善戢士卒、勿縱虜掠。」

translations.literal: Restrain the troops well and do not allow them to plunder freely.
translations.idiomatic: Keep your soldiers under tight discipline and do not let them run wild in pillage.

sentences.zh: 以紇石烈志甯為元帥右監軍，右副元帥完顏謀衍、元帥右監軍完顏福壽召還京師，咸平路總管完顏兀帶復舊職。

translations.literal: Heshilie Zhining was made right army supervisor of the commander-in-chief; Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Mouyan and right army supervisor Wanyan Fushou were recalled to the capital, and Xianping Route administrator Wanyan Udai was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Heshilie Zhining was appointed right army supervisor at headquarters. Wanyan Mouyan and Wanyan Fushou were recalled to the capital, and Wanyan Udai resumed his old post as Xianping Route administrator.

sentences.zh: 謀衍男斜哥在軍中多暴橫，詔押歸本管。

translations.literal: Mouyan's son Xiege had been much given to violence and bullying in the army; an edict ordered him escorted back to his home command.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan's son Xiege had bullied his way through the camp; the court ordered him sent back under guard to his own district.

sentences.zh: 窩斡使所親招節度使移裏堇窟域，窟域執其使送官，與窩斡連戰有功，遷宣武將軍，賜銀五百兩、衣二襲。

translations.literal: Wowa sent a close associate to win over military commissioner Yilieqin Kudiyu; Kudiyu seized the envoy and delivered him to the authorities. For repeated meritorious fighting against Wowa he was promoted to Xuanwu General and granted five hundred taels of silver and two suits of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa sent a trusted man to turn military commissioner Yilieqin Kudiyu. Kudiyu arrested the envoy and handed him over. For steady service against Wowa he was made Xuanwu General and given five hundred taels of silver and two suits of robes.

sentences.zh: 起運在中都弓萬五千、箭一百五十萬赴懿州。

translations.literal: Transport was organized from the Central Capital of fifteen thousand bows and one million five hundred thousand arrows to be sent to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen thousand bows and a million and a half arrows were shipped from the Central Capital to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 平章政事移剌元宜、甯昌軍節度使宗敘入見，詔使自中道卻還軍中，宣諭元宜、謀衍注意經略邊事。

translations.literal: Grand councilor Yila Yuanyi and Ningchang Army military commissioner Zongxu came to audience; they were ordered to turn back midway and return to the army, and Yuanyi and Mouyan were instructed to give careful attention to frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilor Yila Yuanyi and Ningchang commissioner Zongxu were summoned to court, then sent back to the field with orders that Yuanyi and Mouyan focus on managing the frontier war.

sentences.zh: 師久無功，尚書右丞僕散忠義願效死力除邊患，世宗嘉歎。

translations.literal: The army had long been in the field without success; Vice Minister of the Right Pusan Zhongyi offered to exert himself unto death to remove the border calamity, and the Shizong Emperor praised and sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign had dragged on without victory. Vice Minister Pusan Zhongyi volunteered to stake his life on clearing the border threat, and Shizong praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 六月，忠義拜平章政事兼右副元帥，宗敘為兵部尚書，各賜弓矢、具鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zhongyi was appointed grand councilor and concurrently right deputy commander-in-chief; Zongxu was made minister of war; each was granted bow and arrows and a fully saddled and bridled horse from the stables.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhongyi became grand councilor and right deputy commander; Zongxu was named minister of war. Both received bows, quivers, and saddle horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 出內府金銀十萬兩佐軍用。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand taels of gold and silver from the inner treasury were issued to assist military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand taels of gold and silver from the palace treasury were released for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「軍中將士有犯，除連職奏聞，餘依軍法約量決責，有功者依格遷賞。」

translations.literal: An edict said: 'When officers and soldiers in the army commit offenses, except for cases involving linked offices which must be reported to the throne, the rest shall be judged and punished according to military law as circumstances warrant; those with merit shall be promoted and rewarded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'Offenses in the ranks — except where linked offices require a report to the throne — are to be punished under military law as each case warrants. Merit will be rewarded by the usual rules.

sentences.zh: 以大名尹宗尹為河南路統軍使，河南路統軍都監蒲察世傑為西北路副統，賜弓矢佩刀廄馬，從忠義征行。

translations.literal: Zong Yin, prefect of Daming, was made Henan Route commander-in-chief; Henan Route commander-in-chief's supervisor Pucha Shijie was made Northwestern Route deputy commander — both were granted bow and arrows, belt sword, and stable horse, and followed Zhongyi on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yin of Daming was appointed Henan Route commander; Pucha Shijie, his deputy supervisor, became Northwestern Route second-in-command. Both received arms, swords, and horses and marched with Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 詔諭諸軍將士曰：「兵久駐邊陲，蠹費財用無成功，百姓不得休息。

translations.literal: An edict addressed the officers and soldiers of the armies, saying: 'The troops have long been stationed on the frontier, wasting resources without success, and the people cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: The court told every soldier: 'You have sat on the border too long, draining the treasury for nothing, while the people never get peace.

sentences.zh: 今命平章政事僕散忠義兼右副元帥，同心戮力以底戡定。

translations.literal: Now Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi is appointed concurrently right deputy commander-in-chief; with one heart and combined strength you shall bring the campaign to completion and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi now commands as right deputy commander. Stand together and finish this war.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥謀衍罷為同判大宗正事。」

translations.literal: Right Deputy Commander Mouyan was dismissed and made co-administrator of the Imperial Clan Court.'
translations.idiomatic: Right Deputy Commander Mouyan was relieved and made co-administrator of the Imperial Clan Court.'

sentences.zh: 詔居庸關、古北口譏察契丹奸細，捕獲者加官賞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered inspection at Juyong Pass and Gubeikou for Khitan spies; those captured were to receive advancement in rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Guards at Juyong Pass and Gubeikou were ordered to hunt Khitan spies; captors would receive promotion and bounty.

sentences.zh: 萬戶溫蒂罕阿魯帶以兵四千屯古北口，薊州、石門關等處各以五百人守之。

translations.literal: Commander of ten thousand households Wendihan Aludai encamped at Gubeikou with four thousand troops; Jizhou, Shimen Pass, and other places were each garrisoned with five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Aludai took four thousand men to Gubeikou. Jizhou, Shimen Pass, and other posts each received five hundred defenders.

sentences.zh: 海陵末年，阿魯帶為猛安，移剌娜為牌印祗候，起契丹部族兵被執，至是挺身來降。

translations.literal: In the last years of Hailing, Aludai was a meng'an and Yila Na was a seal-bearer and attendant; when Khitan tribal troops were raised they were seized, and now they came forward in person to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hailing, Aludai had been a meng'an and Yila Na a seal attendant. Both were pressed into rebel levies and seized; now they came in person to surrender.

sentences.zh: 世宗以阿魯帶為濟州押軍萬戶，移剌娜為同知濼州事。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor appointed Aludai commander of ten thousand households for garrison troops at Jizhou, and Yila Na co-administrator of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong made Aludai garrison commander of ten thousand at Jizhou and Yila Na co-administrator of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 西南路招討使完顏思敬為都統，賜金牌一、銀牌二，西北路招討使唐括孛古底副之。

translations.literal: Southwestern Route pacification commissioner Wanyan Sijing was made supreme commander and granted one gold tally and two silver tallies; Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Tangqut Ligude served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern pacification commissioner Wanyan Sijing became supreme commander with one gold tally and two silver ones. Tangqut Ligude of the Northwestern Route served under him.

sentences.zh: 以兵五千往會燕子城舊戍軍，視地形沖要或於狗濼屯駐，遠斥候，賊至即戰，不以晝夜為限。

translations.literal: With five thousand troops he was to join the former garrison at Swallow City; according to the terrain's strategic points he might encamp at Gouluo; he was to push scouts far out, fight the moment rebels appeared, and observe no limit of day or night.
translations.idiomatic: He marched five thousand men to join the old garrison at Swallow City, then camped at Gouluo where the ground favored defense. Scouts were pushed far ahead; whenever rebels appeared he was to fight, day or night.

sentences.zh: 詔思敬曰：「契丹賊敗必走山后，可選新馬三千，加芻纇以備追襲。」

translations.literal: An edict to Sijing said: 'When the Khitan rebels are defeated they will surely flee behind the mountains; you may select three thousand fresh horses and add fodder and grain to prepare for pursuit.'
translations.idiomatic: Sijing was told: 'Beaten Khitan rebels will run for the country behind the mountains. Keep three thousand fresh horses fed and ready for the chase.'

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義至軍中。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi arrived at the army.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi reached the front.

sentences.zh: 是時，窩斡西走花道，眾尚八萬。

translations.literal: At this time Wowa was fleeing west along Huadao, and his following still numbered eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa was then fleeing west along Huadao with a host still eighty thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 忠義、高忠建軍與賊遇，萬戶查剌、蒲查為左翼，宗亨統之；

translations.literal: Zhongyi and Gao Zhongjian's army encountered the rebels; commanders of ten thousand households Zhala and Pucha formed the left wing under Zongheng's overall command;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi and Gao Zhongjian met the rebels. Zhala and Pucha led the left wing under Zongheng;

sentences.zh: 宗寧、剌撒為右翼，宗敘統之；

translations.literal: Zongning and Lasa formed the right wing under Zongxu's overall command;
translations.idiomatic: Zongning and Lasa held the right under Zongxu;

sentences.zh: 世傑亦在左翼中，與賊夾河為陣。

translations.literal: Shijie was also in the left wing; the two sides formed battle lines on opposite banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie fought on the left as well. The armies drew up on opposite banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河，以兵四萬餘先犯左翼軍，查剌以六百騎奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed the river and with more than forty thousand troops first struck the left wing; Zhala with six hundred horsemen charged fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels forded the river and hit the left with more than forty thousand men. Zhala answered with six hundred riders and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 複以四萬眾與左翼軍戰，宗亨、世傑七謀克指畫失宜，陣亂敗於賊。

translations.literal: They again fought the left wing with forty thousand; Zongheng and Shijie's seven mouke deployed poorly, the formation broke into disorder, and they were defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: A second wave of forty thousand fell on the left. Zongheng and Shijie's seven mouke misdirected the line; the wing broke and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 世傑挺身投于查剌軍中，賊圍查剌軍，查剌力戰，宗敘以右翼軍來救，賊乃去。

translations.literal: Shijie threw himself bodily into Zhala's force; the rebels surrounded Zhala's army; Zhala fought fiercely; Zongxu came with the right wing to the rescue, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie threw himself into Zhala's ranks as rebels closed around them. Zhala held hard until Zongxu brought the right wing up and the enemy pulled away.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自契丹作逆，有為賊詿誤者，不問如何從賊，但能複業，與免本罪。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Since the Khitan rose in rebellion, those who were misled into following the rebels — regardless of how they joined the enemy — if they can return to their occupations, their original crimes shall be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promised: 'Since the Khitan revolt, anyone misled into rebel service — no matter how he fell in — will be forgiven if he returns to honest work.

sentences.zh: 如能率眾來附，或能殺捕首領而降，或執送賊所扇誘作亂之人，皆與量加官爵。

translations.literal: If they can lead their followers to submit, or kill and capture leaders and surrender, or seize and deliver those whom the rebels incited to rise in disorder, all shall receive measured advancement in rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your people in, kill or capture rebel leaders, or hand over men the rebels stirred up — in every case rank and reward will follow.

sentences.zh: 朕念正隆南征，猛安亡者招還被戮，已命其子孫襲其職。

translations.literal: I recall that during the Zhenglong southern campaign, meng'an who had fled and were summoned back were executed; I have already ordered their sons and grandsons to inherit their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Remember the Zhenglong southern campaign: meng'an who fled and came back were killed. I have already ordered their sons and grandsons to inherit their offices.

sentences.zh: 爾等勿懲前事，故懷遲疑。

translations.literal: You must not take warning from those earlier events and therefore harbor hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let old fears make you hesitate now.

sentences.zh: 賊軍今既破散，山后諸處皆命將士遏其逃路，爾等雖欲不降終將安往？

translations.literal: The rebel army is now broken and scattered; everywhere behind the mountains officers and soldiers have been ordered to block their escape routes — even if you wish not to surrender, where in the end can you go?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host is broken. Every pass behind the mountains is blocked. If you still refuse to yield, where will you run?

sentences.zh: 若猶疑貳，俱就焚滅，悔及矣。」

translations.literal: If you still waver in divided loyalty, you will all be destroyed by fire — and regret will come too late.'
translations.idiomatic: Hold out in divided loyalty and you will all be burned out — too late for regret then.'

sentences.zh: 窩斡自花道西走，僕散忠義、紇石烈志甯以大軍追及於嫋嶺西陷泉。

translations.literal: Wowa fled west from Huadao; Pusan Zhongyi and Heshilie Zhining with the main army overtook him west of Niaoling at Xianquan.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa fled west from Huadao. Pusan Zhongyi and Heshilie Zhining caught him with the main army west of Niaoling at Xianquan.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊軍三萬騎涉水而東。

translations.literal: The next day thirty thousand rebel horsemen waded through the water and moved east.
translations.idiomatic: The next day thirty thousand rebel riders forded the stream and headed east.

sentences.zh: 大軍先據南岡，左翼軍自岡為陣，迤邐而北，步軍繼之，右翼軍繼步軍北引而東，作偃月陣，步軍居中，騎兵據其兩端，使賊不見首尾。

translations.literal: The main army first seized the southern ridge; the left wing formed its line from the ridge, winding northward, with infantry following; the right wing followed the infantry north and then curved east, forming a crescent array — infantry in the center, cavalry holding both ends, so the rebels could not see head or tail.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army took the southern ridge first. The left wing lined the slope and curled north, infantry behind it; the right followed the foot soldiers north, then swung east into a crescent — infantry in the center, cavalry at both horns — so the rebels could not tell front from rear.

sentences.zh: 是日，大霧晦冥，既陣霧開，少頃晴霽，賊見左翼據南岡不敢擊，擊右翼軍，烏延查剌力戰，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: That day dense fog darkened everything; once the formation was set the fog lifted, and shortly the sky cleared; the rebels saw the left wing holding the southern ridge and did not dare attack it, but struck the right wing; Wuyan Zhala fought fiercely and the rebels fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: That day thick fog shrouded the field. As the lines formed the mist lifted and the sky cleared. Seeing the left on the southern ridge, the rebels refused to hit it and turned on the right. Wuyan Zhala fought hard and pushed them back a little.

sentences.zh: 志甯與夾穀清臣、烏林答剌撒、鐸剌合戰，賊大敗，將涉水去，泥濘不得亟渡。

translations.literal: Zhining joined battle with Jiagu Qingchen, Ulinad Lasa, and Dola; the rebels were utterly defeated; about to wade away through the water, they could not cross quickly because of mud and mire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining closed with Jiagu Qingchen, Ulinad Lasa, and Dola and broke the rebels. They tried to flee through the water but the mud held them fast.

sentences.zh: 大軍逐北，人馬相蹂踐而死，不可勝數，陷泉皆平，餘眾蹈籍而過，或奔潰竄匿林莽間。

translations.literal: The main army pursued north; men and horses trampled one another to death beyond counting; Xianquan was levelled flat; the remainder passed over by treading on the fallen, or fled in rout and hid in forest and thicket.
translations.idiomatic: The main force chased them down. Men and horses piled on one another until Xianquan ran level with corpses. Survivors trampled over the dead to escape, or scattered into the woods.

sentences.zh: 大軍踵擊之，俘斬萬計，生擒其弟偽六院司大王嫋。

translations.literal: The main army pressed the pursuit; captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands; his younger brother, the falsely titled Great King of the Six-District Office Niao, was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit went on. Tens of thousands were killed or captured, including Wowa's brother Niao, the rebels' self-styled Great King of the Six Districts.

sentences.zh: 窩斡僅與數騎脫去，鈔兀、清臣追四十餘裏不及，斬千餘級，獲車帳甚眾。

translations.literal: Wowa escaped with only a few riders; Chaowu and Qingchen pursued more than forty li but could not overtake him, beheading more than a thousand and capturing a great many carts and tents.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa got away with only a handful of riders. Chaowu and Qingchen chased forty li without catching him, but cut down more than a thousand and took vast numbers of carts and tents.

sentences.zh: 其母徐輦舉營自落括岡西走，志寧追之，盡獲輜重，俘五萬餘人，雜畜不可勝計。

translations.literal: His mother Xulian moved the entire camp west from Luoguo Ridge; Zhining pursued her, captured all the baggage train, took more than fifty thousand prisoners, and livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa's mother Xulian broke camp west from Luoguo Ridge. Zhining ran her down, seized the entire baggage train, took more than fifty thousand prisoners, and uncounted livestock.

sentences.zh: 偽節度使六及其部族皆降。

translations.literal: The falsely appointed military commissioner Liu and his tribes all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commissioner Liu and his clans submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔北京副統完顏達吉括本部馬，規辦芻糧，仍使達吉為監戰官，錄有功者聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Beijing deputy commander Wanyan Dajiguo to muster horses from his own command, arrange fodder and grain, and also serve as battle supervisor, recording the meritorious and reporting them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing deputy commander Wanyan Dajiguo was ordered to gather his own horses, lay in fodder, serve as battle overseer, and report every man who earned credit.

sentences.zh: 詔選中都、西京兩路新舊軍萬人備守禦，以窩斡敗走，恐或衝突也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered ten thousand men selected from new and old troops of the Central Capital and Western Capital routes to stand ready for defense, because Wowa had been defeated and fled and might yet strike in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand veterans and recruits from the Central and Western Capital routes were picked for home defense — Wowa was beaten but might still lash out.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義使使奏捷，詔略曰：「平章政事右副元帥忠義使使來奏大捷。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi sent envoys to report victory; the edict in summary said: 'Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander Zhongyi's envoys have come to report a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi's messengers brought word of victory. The edict read in part: 'Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander Zhongyi reports a great victory.

sentences.zh: 或被軍俘獲，或自能來服，或無所歸而投拜，或將全屬歸附，或分領家族來降，或嘗受偽命，及自來曾與官軍鬥敵，皆釋其罪。

translations.literal: Whether taken prisoner by the army, coming forward of their own accord to submit, having nowhere to go and therefore bowing in allegiance, bringing all their dependents to attach themselves, leading part of their clans to surrender, or having once received false appointments and even having fought against the government army on their own — all their crimes are released.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners of war, willing submitters, men with nowhere else to turn, whole clans coming over, partial groups surrendering, even those who took rebel titles or once fought us — all are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其散亡人內，除窩斡一身，不以大小官員是何名色，卻來歸附者，亦准釋放。

translations.literal: Among the scattered and displaced, except for Wowa himself, regardless of what rank or title great or small an official may hold, if he returns to submit, release is likewise granted.
translations.idiomatic: Of the scattered rebels, every man who comes in is freed — whatever rank he held — except Wowa himself.

sentences.zh: 有能誅捕窩斡，或於不從招納亡去人內誅捕以來，及或能率眾于掌軍官及隨處官司投降者，並給官賞。

translations.literal: Whoever can kill or capture Wowa, or among those who fled rather than accept summons kill or capture and deliver them, or can lead followers to surrender to the camp commander or local officials — all shall receive official reward.
translations.idiomatic: Kill or capture Wowa, seize fugitives who refused the summons, or bring your people to any camp commander or local office — in every case there will be rank and reward.

sentences.zh: 各路撫納來者，毋得輒加侵損。

translations.literal: On every route those who receive and settle newcomers must not on their own authority add injury or harm.
translations.idiomatic: Every route that receives surrendering men must not harass or rob them.

sentences.zh: 無資給者，不以是何路分，隨有糧處安置，仍官為養濟。」

translations.literal: Those without means of support, regardless of which route they belong to, shall be settled wherever grain is available, and the government shall still provide relief.'
translations.idiomatic: Men without supplies are to be settled wherever grain can be found, on any route, and fed at public expense.'

sentences.zh: 窩斡收合散卒萬餘人，遂入奚部，以諸奚自益，時時出兵寇速魯古澱、古北口、興化之間。

translations.literal: Wowa gathered more than ten thousand scattered soldiers, then entered Xi territory and strengthened himself with various Xi tribes; from time to time he sent troops to raid between Sulugu Marsh, Gubeikou, and Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Wowa regrouped more than ten thousand stragglers and slipped into Xi country, swelling his ranks with Xi tribesmen. He raided between Sulugu Marsh, Gubeikou, and Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕阿魯帶守古北口，與戰敗焉。

translations.literal: Wendihan Aludai defended Gubeikou and was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Aludai held Gubeikou and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 詔完顏謀衍、蒲察烏裏雅、蒲察蒲盧渾以兵三千，合舊屯兵五千，擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wanyan Mouyan, Pucha Wuliya, and Pucha Puluhun to take three thousand troops, join the former garrison of five thousand, and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Mouyan, Pucha Wuliya, and Pucha Puluhun were sent with three thousand men to join the five thousand already on station and hit Wowa's force.

sentences.zh: 詔守顏思敬以所部兵入奚地，會大軍討窩斡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wanyan Sijing to lead his own troops into Xi territory and join the main army in campaigning against Wowa.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sijing was ordered into Xi country with his command to link up with the main force hunting Wowa.

sentences.zh: 賊黨霿𩃭河猛安蒲速越遣人至帥府約降，詔令擒捕窩斡，許以官賞。

translations.literal: Among the rebels, meng'an Pusuyue of the Menglong River sent men to the command headquarters to negotiate surrender; an edict ordered him to capture Wowa, with official reward promised.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel meng'an Pusuyue of the Menglong River sent envoys to headquarters to discuss surrender. He was told to seize Wowa and promised rank and reward.

sentences.zh: 賊將降者甚眾。

translations.literal: Very many rebel officers came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel officers surrendered in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 其散走者聞詔書招降，亦多降者。

translations.literal: Those who had scattered and fled, hearing the edict summoning surrender, also surrendered in large numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered fugitives who heard the surrender edict came in as well.

sentences.zh: 其餘多疾疫而死，無複鬥志。

translations.literal: The remainder mostly died of pestilence and no longer had any will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the rest died of plague and lost the will to fight.

sentences.zh: 窩斡自度勢窮，乃謀自羊城道西京奔夏國，大軍追之益急，其眾複多亡去，度不得西，乃北走沙陀間。

translations.literal: Wowa judged his position hopeless and planned to flee west through Yangcheng toward the Western Capital and on to the Xia state; the main army pressed the pursuit ever harder, and many of his followers again deserted; seeing he could not go west, he fled north among the Shatuo wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his cause lost, Wowa planned to run west through Yangcheng toward the Western Capital and into Xia territory. The pursuit tightened and more men slipped away. Blocked from the west, he turned north into the Shatuo country.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省：「凡脅從之家被俘掠遂致離散，宜從改正。

translations.literal: An edict to the Imperial Secretariat said: 'As for households of those coerced to follow who were captured and plundered and thereby scattered, correction should be applied according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was told: 'Families of men forced into rebel service, then captured and scattered, are to be set right as each case requires.

sentences.zh: 將士往往藏匿其人，有司檢括分付。」

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers often hide such persons; the authorities shall search them out and restore them to their proper places.'
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers often hide these people. Officials must search them out and return them to their families.'

sentences.zh: 監軍志寧獲賊稍合住，釋而弗殺，縱還賊中，使誘其親近捕窩斡以自效，許以官賞。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Zhining captured the rebel Shaohezhu, released him without killing him, and sent him back into rebel ranks to induce his close associates to capture Wowa as proof of merit, with official reward promised.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Zhining took the rebel Shaohezhu alive, freed him, and sent him back to turn his comrades against Wowa — capture the leader and earn rank and reward.

sentences.zh: 九月庚子，稍合住與神獨斡執窩斡，詣右都臨完顏思敬降，並獲其母徐輦及其妻、子、子婦、弟、侄，盡收偽金銀牌印。

translations.literal: On gengzi of the ninth month Shaohezhu and Shenduwo seized Wowa and went to surrender to right army supervisor Wanyan Sijing; they also captured his mother Xulian and his wife, sons, daughters-in-law, younger brother, and nephews, and recovered all the false gold and silver tallies and seals.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the ninth month Shaohezhu and Shenduwo seized Wowa and surrendered to Wanyan Sijing. They took his mother Xulian, wife, sons, daughters-in-law, brother, and nephews, and recovered every false gold tally, silver tally, and seal.

sentences.zh: 唐括孛古底獲前胡裏改節度使什溫及其家屬。

translations.literal: Tangqut Ligude captured the former Huligai military commissioner Shiwen and his family.
translations.idiomatic: Tangqut Ligude took the former Huligai commissioner Shiwen and his household.

sentences.zh: 西北路招討使李家奴獲偽樞密使逐斡等三十餘人，複與猛安泥本婆果追偽監軍那也至天成縣，那也乃降，乃獲偽都元帥醜哥及金牌一、銀牌五。

translations.literal: Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Li Jianu captured more than thirty men including the falsely appointed privy commissioner Zhuwo; he again joined meng'an Niben Boguo in pursuing the false army supervisor Naye to Tiancheng County — Naye then surrendered, and they captured the false supreme commander Chouge together with one gold tally and five silver tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern pacification commissioner Li Jianu seized more than thirty rebels, including the false privy commissioner Zhuwo. With meng'an Niben Boguo he chased false supervisor Naye to Tiancheng; Naye yielded, and they took the false supreme commander Chouge plus one gold tally and five silver ones.

sentences.zh: 志甯與清臣、宗甯、速哥等追餘黨至燕子城，盡得其黨。

translations.literal: Zhining with Qingchen, Zongning, Suge, and others pursued the remaining rebels to Swallow City and captured their entire party.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining, Qingchen, Zongning, Suge, and the rest ran the remnant to Swallow City and took them all.

sentences.zh: 前至抹拔裏達之地，悉獲之，逆党遂平。

translations.literal: Advancing to Mobalida they captured them all; the rebel faction was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Mobalida, rounded up everyone left, and the rebellion was finished.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，皇太子率百官上表賀。

translations.literal: On jiachen the crown prince led the hundred officials in submitting a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the crown prince led the court in a memorial of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔天下。

translations.literal: On yisi an edict was issued to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the victory was proclaimed to the realm.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，完顏思敬獻俘于京師，窩斡梟首於市，磔其手足，分懸諸京府。

translations.literal: On xinhai Wanyan Sijing presented captives at the capital; Wowa's head was exposed in the marketplace, his limbs dismembered, and the parts hung separately in various capitals and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Wanyan Sijing presented the prisoners in the capital. Wowa's head was hung in the market, his limbs quartered and displayed in cities across the realm.

sentences.zh: 其母徐輦及妻子皆戮之。

translations.literal: His mother Xulian and his wife and sons were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Xulian, wife, and sons were put to death.

sentences.zh: 契丹降人皆拘其器仗，貧不能自給者官為養濟。

translations.literal: Khitan who surrendered were all required to surrender their weapons; those too poor to support themselves were maintained by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendering Khitan were disarmed. Those too poor to live on their own were fed at public expense.

sentences.zh: 括裏、紮八率眾南走，詔左宣徽使宗亨追及之。

translations.literal: Kuoli and Zhaba led their followers south in flight; an edict ordered left palace intendant Zongheng to pursue and overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and Zhaba fled south with their bands. Left palace intendant Zongheng was sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 紮八詐稱降，宗亨信其言，遂不與戰。

translations.literal: Zhaba falsely claimed he wished to surrender; Zongheng believed his words and therefore did not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba feigned surrender. Zongheng believed him and held his men back.

sentences.zh: 紮八紿之曰：「括裏驚走，願追之。」

translations.literal: Zhaba deceived him, saying: 'Kuoli fled in panic; I wish to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba lied: 'Kuoli bolted in fright. Let me chase him.

sentences.zh: 宗亨縱紮八去。

translations.literal: Zongheng let Zhaba go.
translations.idiomatic: Zongheng released Zhaba.

sentences.zh: 益都猛安欲以所部追括裏、紮八，宗亨恐分其功，不聽，而縱軍士取賊所棄資囊人畜而自有之。

translations.literal: The Yidu meng'an wished to pursue Kuoli and Zhaba with his own command; Zongheng, fearing his merit would be divided, would not allow it, but let his soldiers take for themselves the rebels' abandoned goods, bags, livestock, and people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yidu meng'an asked to chase Kuoli and Zhaba with his own men. Zongheng refused — he did not want to share the credit — and let his soldiers loot the rebels' abandoned goods, livestock, and captives for themselves.

sentences.zh: 括裏、紮入由是得亡去，遂奔于宋。

translations.literal: Kuoli and Zhaba thereby escaped, and fled to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and Zhaba got away and fled to Song territory.

sentences.zh: 宗亨降甯州剌史。

translations.literal: Zongheng was demoted to prefect of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongheng was reduced to prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後，宋李世輔用括裏、紮八，遂取宿州，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Song's Li Shifu employed Kuoli and Zhaba, and thereby took Suzhou — a considerable border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Later Song general Li Shifu used Kuoli and Zhaba to seize Suzhou, and they became a serious border nuisance.

sentences.zh: 神獨斡除同知安化軍節度使，稍合住除同知震武軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Shenduwo was appointed co-military commissioner of the Anhua Army; Shaohezhu was appointed co-administrator of affairs of the Zhenwu Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shenduwo became co-commissioner of the Anhua Army; Shaohezhu co-commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 大定六年，點檢司奏，親軍中有逆黨子弟，請一切罷去。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dading the Palace Inspection Office memorialized that among the personal guard were sons and younger brothers of rebel faction members, and requested that all be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 6 the Palace Inspection Office reported sons of rebel families in the personal guard and asked that all be removed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「身預逆黨者罷之，餘勿問。」

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Those who personally joined the rebel faction are to be dismissed; the rest are not to be investigated.'
translations.idiomatic: The reply was blunt: 'Dismiss only those who joined the rebels themselves. Leave the rest alone.'

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金人以燕山與宋，遂啟張覺跳樑之心，覺豈為宋者哉，蓋欲乘時以徼利耳。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the Jin gave the Yan Mountains to the Song, they thereby awakened in Zhang Jue the heart of a cornered rat leaping at the beam — yet was Jue truly for the Song? He merely wished to seize the moment and grasp profit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Ceding the Yan Mountains to the Song stirred Zhang Jue's desperate ambition — but Jue was no friend of Song. He only meant to profit from the moment.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹從宗望追天祚，曾不遺餘力，功成驕溢，自取誅滅，咈哉。

translations.literal: Yelü Yudu followed Zongwang in pursuing Tianzuo and spared no effort whatsoever; when success was achieved he grew proud and excessive and brought execution upon himself — alas, how perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yudu followed Zongwang against Tianzuo and held nothing back. Victory made him arrogant, and he walked himself to the execution ground — a bitter end.

sentences.zh: 正隆佳兵，契丹作難，《傳》曰：「夫兵猶火也，弗戢將自焚。」

translations.literal: Zhenglong prized arms; the Khitan rose in calamity. The Commentary says: 'War is like fire — if it is not checked, it will burn the user.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglong glorified war, and the Khitan revolt answered. As the Commentary says: 'War is fire; fail to bank it and you burn yourself.'

sentences.zh: 可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Is this not a warning to be heeded!'
translations.idiomatic: Let that be a warning!'
